items.title: Universal link between structural relaxation and self-diffusion in simple supercooled liquids
authors: Mingyu Zhu, Xinyu Chang, Licun Fu, Yiming Zheng, Lijin Wang
items.summary: Despite a vigorous effort, a comprehensive and satisfactory understanding of the dynamics underlying the glass transition in finite-dimensional systems has not yet emerged. One key hallmark of supercooled liquids approaching the glass transition is the breakdown of the classical Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation, manifested as the decoupling between the self-diffusion coefficient and structural relaxation time, commonly described by a fractional SE relation. Whether and how the fractional SE exponents vary remains an ongoing debate, even for the simplest supercooled liquids. In this work, we numerically establish a universal relation between the self-diffusion coefficient and structural relaxation time by introducing characteristic scales that are revealed under the condition of constant dynamical heterogeneity. Moreover, this universal relation could also capture literature data for supercooled water and silica. Remarkably, we find that the fractional SE exponent is invariant across various supercooled liquids studied spanning a wide range of fragility, thereby challenging the prevailing view that the fractional SE exponent is correlated with fragility. Our study demonstrates that investigating dynamical heterogeneity yields more valuable insights into understanding glassy dynamics than expected.

items.title: Noise-Induced Restoration of Entropy Concavity Near Gaussian Equilibrium
items.summary: We study a quantitative form of noise-induced restoration of entropy concavity for one-dimensional nonequilibrium states relaxing toward a Gaussian thermal equilibrium. A partially thermalized state is modeled by $X_q=\sqrt q\,X+\sqrt{1-q}\,G$, where $G$ is Gaussian equilibrium noise and $q$ is the retained signal fraction. For two independently prepared copies we ask when the entropy of the mixed state $h(\sqrt{1-t}\,X_q+\sqrt t\,Y_q)$ is concave in the mixing parameter. The problem is motivated by entropy geometry along Ornstein--Uhlenbeck/Fokker--Planck relaxation, where the relative score is the nonequilibrium thermodynamic force and relative Fisher information is entropy-production rate. We derive an exact symmetric endpoint-curvature formula, separating a nonnegative Ornstein--Uhlenbeck restoring term from a fourth-cumulant correction, and extend it to nonsmooth generalized-Gaussian states $e^{-a|x|^p}$ for $p>3/2$. For half thermalization of a symmetric log-concave input, posterior-variance identities give a quantitative outer-region theorem confining any endpoint obstruction to two explicitly bounded near-equilibrium sectors. We also give spectral and MMSE reformulations of the auxiliary inequality $A\ge2\delta$, prove it in an explicit nonlinear neighborhood of Gaussian equilibrium, and show how it sharpens the endpoint bounds. The main all-mixing result concerns the leading symmetric non-Gaussian Hermite mode: for $p_a=\phiG(1+a\He_4)$, $0 <q\le4/7$ for this explicit nonequilibrium family. Numerical searches over broader log-concave families are reported only as supporting evidence.

items.title: QMBL: the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard. A live record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians
items.summary: In condensed matter physics, scientists explore phase diagrams of matter through various methods (analysis, numerics, experiment) and achieve consensus when enough methods agree. The quality of variational results for quantum many-body ground states is mainly judged by energy values and respective errors. Here, we present QMBL, the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard (https://www.qmbl.org), serving as the energy layer of the scientific consensus. It is a maintained, interactive record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians. The latest release v0.4.0 holds 1434 energies on 395 instances of six model families and collects all of the community's efforts into one view. Of those instances 153 have no exact solution and any new record serves as a direct improvement to an open science problem. They are the targets of a companion benchmark, QMBL: Open Problems.

items.title: Thermodynamics of coupled electromagnetic and mass fields
items.summary: We formulate a unified thermodynamic framework for chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport by extending the Gibbs--Duhem relation to include kinetic free-energy contributions associated with material and field motion. The resulting kinetic Gibbs--Duhem relation establishes a thermodynamic connection between free-energy variations, generalized chemical potentials, pressure, and transport momentum, while preserving the invariance of the system free energy under changes of reference frame. Within a Lagrangian formulation of free-energy evolution, the relation provides a common structure for diffusion, momentum transport, and electromagnetic dynamics. For nonuniform chemical systems, the framework recovers the coupling between Cahn--Hilliard dynamics and the Korteweg stress arising from composition gradients. Its extension to electromagnetic systems incorporates electric, magnetic, charge, and mechanical contributions into the same thermodynamic formulation, yielding a unified description of electromagnetic and momentum evolution. The framework further separates dissipative from nondissipative transport and establishes a common thermodynamic form for mechanical and electromagnetic propagation. In the isentropic limit, the characteristic propagation velocity is determined by the derivative of the thermodynamic pressure with respect to density, yielding the speed of sound for mechanical systems and the speed of light for electromagnetic systems. These results show that kinetic contributions can be incorporated consistently into the Gibbs--Duhem framework, providing a common thermodynamic basis for coupled chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport without introducing separate thermodynamic principles for each mechanism.

items.title: Visualizing surface-reaction-driven chloride migration and cascading failure in sulfide solid electrolytes
authors: Xiaoya He, Haoran Zhang, Xinyang Yue, Hang Liu, Zian Mao, Jialong Wang, Min Liu, Shufen Chu, Liwei Chen, Zhaoxin Yu, Xi Liu, Chuying Ouyang, Ziyang Ning, Yujun Xie
items.summary: Moisture instability of sulfide solid electrolytes limits practical use in all-solid-state batteries. Spatially resolving gas--solid reactions during moisture exposure remains challenging. Here, cryogenic four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (cryo-4D-STEM) maps nanoscale degradation in low- and high-Cl argyrodite electrolytes, Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl and Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\). Li\(_6\)PS\(_5\)Cl undergoes predominantly surface-localized degradation that progressively extends inward, whereas Li\(_{5.5}\)PS\(_{4.5}\)Cl\(_{1.5}\) exhibits rapid interior amorphization accompanied by outward chloride redistribution. Density functional theory calculations indicate a lower chloride-migration barrier along the modeled pathway in the higher-Cl composition, while chloride removal and vacancy formation distort the PS\(_4^{3-}\) framework and may destabilize the lattice. Surface treatment suppresses detectable large-scale chloride segregation and improves moisture tolerance, retaining 99.9% of the capacity measured at the start of 0.33 C cycling after 150 cycles. These results identify chloride redistribution as a key process in degradation propagation and suggest a route toward moisture-tolerant solid-state batteries.

items.title: Synergistic Self-Driven Nanoconfinement and Dynamical Heterogeneity in Deeply Supercooled "No Man's Land" Water
items.summary: The 150--235 K ``no man's land'' (NML) of deeply supercooled water is a highly debated regime where rapid crystallization hinders experimental observation of the hypothesized liquid-liquid phase transition. Using TIP4P/2005 molecular dynamics simulations, we uncover a structurally and dynamically heterogeneous state at ambient pressure that exhibits novel physical features. Our results demonstrate that this low-density state ($\rho \approx 0.925$ g/cm$^3$) is a unique supercooled liquid, distinct from both glassy and spinodal states. Specifically, it emerges as a stable, structurally arrested phase driven by a self-generated ``soft skeleton'' of nanoclusters. This network forms an intrinsic nanoporous structure that imposes nanoconfinement on the remaining fluid, proving that NML confinement can be an entirely self-driven phenomenon. Finally, we resolve the temperature-dependent, nonlinear behavior of density and compressibility, highlighting a structurally driven anomaly that clarifies the thermodynamics of deep supercooling. Collectively, this work provides a transformative structural framework for understanding the anomalous nature of water within the NML.

items.title: Semiclassical Analysis of Wave Dynamics via Wigner Transforms: Applications to the Quantum Harmonic, Anharmonic, and Dirac Oscillator
items.summary: In this Master's thesis, we give a pedagogical introduction to the semiclassical analysis of wave dynamics in single-band and multi-band systems. We show how the semiclassical evolutions of Wigner functions can approximate the dynamics of wave packet centers and wave packet deformations. Three systems of increasing complexity are considered: the quantum harmonic oscillator and the quantum anharmonic oscillator as single-band systems, and the Dirac oscillator as a two-band system. We explain the origins of the first-order semiclassical corrections (Moyal, Littlejohn-Flynn, and Berry) in the equations of motion and examine their effects on predictive accuracy. Another focus is set on the conditions for validity of the semiclassical analysis. For both the quantum anharmonic and the Dirac oscillators, a dimensionless parameter controlling the accuracy of the approximation is identified. In multi-band systems, the formalism applies only to states within a single adiabatic subspace, which, for the Dirac oscillator, corresponds to an energy branch. This motivates the construction of single-branch almost coherent states: approximately Gaussian wave packets formed by superpositions of states from a single energy branch. Their centers undergo oscillations with an aperiodic envelope. These states enable comparison between semiclassical Wigner function evolution and the commonly used Sundaram-Niu formalism. We show that semiclassical Wigner function evolution captures deformation-related dynamics, including the initial decay of oscillations, which the Sundaram-Niu formalism cannot describe by construction. Additionally, exact quantum evolution reveals partial relocalization of these single-branch almost coherent states, a phenomenon that cannot be captured by the semiclassical evolution.

items.title: Magnetic tunnel junctions of twisted La2/3Sr1/3MnO3 freestanding bilayers
authors: Kota Kanda, Shiho Irie, Kodai Niitsu, Masayuki Ochi, Takumi Yamazaki, Kouta Kondou, Kohei Ueda, Takeshi Seki, Jobu Matsuno, Junichi Shiogai
items.summary: Transition metal oxides (TMOs) host a variety of emergent spintronic or multiferroic functionalities owing to the intricate interplay between lattice, orbital, charge, and spin degrees of freedom. Recent advances in epitaxial lift-off and dry transfer techniques using water-soluble sacrificial layers enables stacking and twisting of freestanding membranes of such strongly correlated oxides, providing even richer physical properties and functionalities. To date, the twisted junctions of TMOs have been mainly investigated in insulators, focusing on their structural and dielectric properties. Here, we demonstrate that the twisted bilayer membranes of La2/3Sr1/3MnO3, a prototypical half-metallic ferromagnetic metal TMO, offer a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) with their van der Waals (vdW) gap acting as a tunnel barrier. The twisted junctions of La2/3Sr1/3MnO3 exhibit tunnelling magnetoresistance (TMR) effect with respect to relative orientation of magnetizations of top and bottom membranes. In addition, high-field magnetoresistance shows uniaxial anisotropy, which can be assigned to tunnelling anisotropic magnetoresistance (TAMR) effect reflecting rhombohedral distortion of fully-relaxed La2/3Sr1/3MnO3. The demonstration of TMR and TAMR effects suggests that spin and in-plane momentum degrees of freedom of 3d electrons are conserved across the twisted junctions of TMOs, opening a new avenue for realizing strongly correlated twistronics utilizing electron coherence through tunnelling processes.

items.title: Intercalation of Ultrathin Ferromagnetic Iron Films at the Graphene/SiC Interface
authors: Niels R\"osch, Rico Ehrler, Stefanie Suzanne Brinkman, Xin Liang Tan, Anders Christian Mathisen, Marc Stevens, Sascha Hermann, Olav Hellwig, Philip Sch\"adlich, Hendrik Bentmann, Susanne Wolff, Thomas Seyller, Fabian G\"ohler
items.summary: The intercalation of high-quality PASG-grown (polymer-assisted sublimation growth) zero-layer graphene on 4H-SiC(0001) with iron is studied using a deposition-and-annealing approach. We find that unlike other metals, Fe does not easily intercalate, and the intercalation procedure has to be balanced with the formation of iron silicides and graphitic carbon at the interface. After successful intercalation, the ultrathin iron films are protected against oxidation by the covering graphene sheet, and retain ferromagnetic behaviour with an in-plane easy axis even at room temperature. When exposed to a selenium-rich atmosphere at elevated temperatures, an almost complete exchange of Fe by Se is observed, imposing a major restriction for the formation of multi-element 2D compounds via sequential intercalation schemes.

items.title: A Physics-based and Geometry-aware Reduced-order Framework for Accelerated Part-Scale Thermomechanical Simulation of Additive Friction Stir Deposition Process
items.summary: Additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) is attractive for naval and aerospace sustainment because it enables high rate, solid state near net shape fabrication and repair of large metallic components. However, full part scale thermomechanical simulations remain computationally demanding because of the moving heat source, progressive material deposition, and evolving geometry. This work presents a physics-based and geometry-aware reduced order framework for rapid prediction of temperature and residual stress fields in part scale AFSD builds. The transient temperature field is represented using a tensor product quadratic B spline basis on a fixed Cartesian background grid, while arbitrary part geometries are embedded using a signed distance function (SDF) and a smooth material indicator. Residual stresses are recovered through an inherent strain formulation in which an offline thermo elasto plastic representative volume element (RVE) simulation supplies a calibrated eigenstrain field that is spatially scaled using the part scale peak temperature history. The thermal formulation is evaluated against published numerical and experimental AFSD data and two sample multilayer builds are simulated as demonstrations. For a four layer thin-wall build, the thermal solution requires approximately 22 s compared to 806 s for the finite element model, while the complete thermo-mechanical framework requires approximately 86.4 s compared to 2,406 s. For a larger 20 layer hollow cylindrical build, the reduced order thermal simulations requires 0.148 to 0.152 h compared with 1.8 h for the finite element model, corresponding to thermal speed-ups of approximately 11.8 to 12.2 times. The complete thermomechanical framework requires 0.346 h compared to 5.4 h for the full finite element analysis, providing an overall speed-up of approximately 15.6 times.

items.title: Automated end-station at the soft X-ray beamline featuring robotic air-to-ultrahigh-vacuum sample transfer, scanning probe spectroscopy, and machine learning analysis
authors: Keita Hiromori, Masashige Miyamoto, Masafumi Horio, Takeru Nakashima, Yasunobu Ando, Masato Kotsugi, Iwao Matsuda
items.summary: Driven by the growing integration of artificial intelligence and robotics in experimental science, we redefine the execution of user experiments at synchrotron soft X-ray beamlines by developing a highly automated end-station that can be operated without on-site staff. Installed at beamline BL08U of NanoTerasu, the system comprises four chamber units and two robots that automatically transfer samples from ambient air to an ultrahigh vacuum measurement stage for spectroscopic evaluations, before returning them to their original locations post-measurement. Soft X-ray absorption spectra are automatically acquired once programmed by scanning the micro-focused beam over the designated sample area, followed by automated evaluation using machine learning techniques such as principal-component analysis, multidimensional scaling, t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding, and uniform manifold approximation and projection. The high-throughput data are systematically accumulated in the database for remote user examination. This unstaffed end-station provides efficient beamtime for users and allows beamline scientists/technicians to pursue more human and creative endeavors.

items.title: Mean-Field Dynamics of the Bose-Hubbard Model in High Dimension
authors: Shahnaz Farhat, Denis P\'erice, S\"oren Petrat
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The Bose-Hubbard model effectively describes bosons on a lattice with on-site interactions and nearest-neighbour hopping, serving as a foundational framework for understanding strong particle interactions and the superfluid to Mott insulator transition. This paper aims to rigorously establish the validity of a mean-field approximation for the dynamics of quantum systems in high dimension, using the Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice as a case study. We prove a trace norm estimate between the one-lattice-site reduced density of the Schr\"odinger dynamics and the mean-field dynamics in the limit of large dimension. Here, the mean-field approximation is in the hopping amplitude and not in the interaction, leading to a very rich and non-trivial mean-field equation. This mean-field equation does not only describe the condensate, as is the case when the mean-field description comes from a large particle number limit averaging out the interaction, but it allows for a phase transition to a Mott insulator since it contains the full non-trivial interaction. Our work is a rigorous justification of a simple case of the highly successful dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for bosons, which somewhat surprisingly yields many qualitatively correct results in three dimensions.

items.title: Geometric heat pumping on a quantum processor
authors: Ger\'onimo J. Caselli, Luis O. Manuel, Liliana Arrachea, Pablo S. Cornaglia
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Geometric heat pumping is the transfer of energy between reservoirs at equal temperature where the heat exchanged in an adiabatic cycle depends only on the driving contour in parameter space. We implement this mechanism on a superconducting quantum processor using a collision model, where a driven qubit interacts repeatedly with two ancilla qubits that are prepared in thermal states and emulate the reservoirs. Energy measurements before and after each interaction provide a calorimetric record of the heat exchanged with each reservoir. By reversing the driving contour, we extract a heat contribution associated with pumping. Its dependence on the period and on the contour follows exact simulations of the collision model, without adjustable parameters, and approaches in the slow-driving regime the geometric limit of the corresponding Lindblad dynamics.

items.title: How to compare and strengthen research systems
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03309-3 Analysing national research systems by using open-access data and new methods can help countries to learn from each other.

items.title: A randomized trial of supported versus self-fitting over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78833-x In a multicenter pragmatic trial, structured primary care physician or remote audiologist support improved the benefits and sustained use of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults compared with self-fitting.

items.title: Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78423-x This study models the collapse of ice mélange in glacial fjords in response increasing submarine melt rates. It shows that perennial mélange today is vulnerable to collapse subject to increasing melt, potentially accelerating glacier mass loss.

items.title: Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78435-7 Cytotoxic lymphocytes-derived granzyme-A (GZMA) cleaves the pore-forming protein GSDMB to trigger pyroptotic killing in target cells. Here, the authors show that the homodimer GZMA provides dual exosites and active sites, allowing specific recognition and process of GSDMB in a trans mode.

items.title: Laminated structure design accommodates thermal expansion mismatch for mechanically and thermally dual-stable thermoelectric contacts
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78685-5 This work proposes a design strategy based on laminated metals, in which thermal expansion of the barrier layer is tailored to regulate interfacial stress–diffusion coupling, enabling mechanically and thermally dual-stable thermoelectric contacts.

items.title: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78772-7 Macrophages tightly control their phagocytic capacity, limiting intracellular overcrowding. However, the molecular details of this adaptive response remain undefined. Here, the authors combine live in vivo imaging with fly genetics and show that, in phagocytic Drosophila macrophages, mechanical and molecular adaptations of the nucleus to the indenting phagosomal cargoes are required to sustain macrophage phagocytosis in vivo.

items.title: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78785-2 Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of light transport phenomena, shaped by reflection, scattering and absorption processes. Here, we introduce a workflow that integrates ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to autonomously design photoreactors in a closed-loop manner, achieving high photon capture and uniform irradiation.

items.title: Projected intensification of soil salinization in global drylands under future aridity increase
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78622-6 This global study assesses how future increases in aridity will reshape dryland soil salinity patterns through the 21st century under four climate scenarios, evaluating compound future exposure to salinization and its threats to water-food security.

items.title: Polymer-agnostic crosslinking enables robust high-temperature dielectrics for energy storage
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78724-1 In capacitive energy storage systems, crosslinking can improve polymer electrothermal stability, but conventional approaches rely on polymer-specific chemistries and often introduce defects that compromise insulating performance. Here the authors present a polymer-agnostic crosslinking platform based on nitrene mediated C–H insertion that improves performance and stability across a wide range of commercial dielectric polymers.

items.title: Bridging microwaves and light
items.summary: Nature Materials, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02763-8 Strong coupling between magnons and excitons in CrSBr enables microwave-to-optical transduction, offering a route towards efficient conversion between otherwise disparate frequency regimes.

items.title: Bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnets enable untethered organ monitoring
items.summary: Nature Materials, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02759-4 A bioresorbable, metal-free molecular magnet for wireless deep-tissue sensing is reported that enables continuous cardiac monitoring and injectable organ tracking in vivo before the material safely degrades.

items.title: Ionic switching between supermagnetic states
items.summary: Supermagnetic states are typically set during synthesis. Changing and retaining these states requires sustained external stimulus. Without resynthesis or continued stimulus, we show, for the first time, a reversible magneto-ionic switching between superferromagnetic (SFM) and superspin-glass (SSG) states using room-temperature Li-ion transport. We utilize the incomplete lithiation of NiO into nanoscale Ni and Li2O to switch between the states. Lithiation generates a fragmented nano-Ni network that strengthens dipolar interactions and promotes SFM order with stronger memory and higher room-temperature moments. Delithiation partially regenerates NiO and drives the system into an SSG state with higher low-temperature coercivity and sharper temperature-selective memory. The interconversion between SFM and SSG persists at all measured subsequent lithiation-delithiation cycles, creating a general framework for supermagnetic switching.

items.title: Strengthened second law for periodic processes
items.summary: We derive a lower bound on the entropy production of any physical system that evolves as a periodic process. Crucially, this lower bound is completely independent of the physical mechanism implementing the periodic dynamics; it follows purely from the definition of entropy production and the fact that whatever the physical mechanism is, it repeats in each period. In particular, the lower bound holds in both Markovian and non-Markovian systems, in systems that obey or violate (local) detailed balance, and even if the underlying physical mechanism uses currently unknown laws of physics. Moreover, the bound is strictly positive whenever the dynamics is not logically invertible. In this breadth of applicability, our bound is a strict strengthening of the second law. We illustrate our bound for spins coupled to two heat reservoirs and for finite automata.

items.title: A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses
items.summary: We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.

items.title: Critical Free-Energy Variance in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
items.summary: We study the variance of the free energy in the Gaussian Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at zero external field. For every system size and inverse temperature $β>0$, we prove $2N^2\operatorname{Var} F_N^{\mathrm{off}}(β) \le \logχ+(β^2-1)(χ-1), χ=N\mathbb{E}\langle R_{1,2}^2\rangle_β$, where $R_{1,2}$ is the replica overlap and $F_N^{\mathrm{off}}=N^{-1}\log Z_N^{\mathrm{off}}$ omits diagonal disorder. The proof uses an exact identity for the edges incident to one spin, Schur complements, and Gaussian disorder interpolation. At criticality the bound reduces to $2N^2\operatorname{Var} F_N^{\mathrm{off}}(1)\le\logχ$. An explicit nonnegative integral measures its gap. A second decomposition relates this gap to a mixed cubic overlap functional. Existing moment and cavity estimates imply that its required integral is bounded. Critical susceptibility asymptotics give the sharp logarithmic upper coefficient and show that the gap converges exactly when the variance has a constant term. We extend an entropy bound throughout bounded critical temperature windows and establish overlap moment stability on a smaller interval.

items.title: Gap edge eigenpairs from density matrix purification using moments of the Dirac distribution
items.summary: In this work, we propose a simple method to resolve the eigenstates located at the band gap edges of an electronic eigenspectrum using only the quasi-purified one-particle density matrix as input. The theoretical framework relies on the decomposition of the occupation number variance into a particle and a hole moment. These moments, when purified using power narrowing iterations, allow us to isolate the highest occupied and lowest unoccupied single-state projectors, \colp{giving ready access} to the corresponding eigenpairs. We demonstrate that when degeneracy is encountered, power narrowing remains able to deliver relevant mixed states. From a benchmark of selected molecules, we show that the method is robust and efficient since it requires from four to sixteen matrix-matrix multiplications in the worst case. The possibility of reducing the computational cost using the Lanczos subspace approach is discussed. The algorithm simplicity of power narrowing makes it very easy to implement in electronic structure codes or libraries already featuring Fermi operator expansion or density matrix purification.

items.title: Anyonic Neural Network Wavefunctions
items.summary: The macroscopic behavior of a non-interacting gas of Abelian anyons has remained unsettled for many decades. Prior numerical methods employing exact diagonalization in the continuum and on the plane have been limited to small system sizes, at most $N = 4$ anyons. Using the rapidly developing technology of neural network wavefunctions, we develop variational ansatze appropriate for studying continuum models of the Abelian anyon gas. The neural network architecture, which we call "AnyNet", is capable of exactly enforcing the non-analytic short-distance behavior induced by the anyonic statistics. We demonstrate excellent agreement with exact diagonalization for $N=4$ anyons, obtain accurate results up to $N = 16$ for intermediate statistics, and study up to $N=20$ for almost-fermionic anyons, matching perturbative results within a 0.4% discrepancy. We use this methodology to study anyons in a harmonic trap, and anyonic atoms as a model for anyon binding to impurities. We study the structure of anyonic wavefunctions as the statistics parameter is varied. We focus on the single-particle density, the pair density, the angular momentum, and the scaling of the wavefunction as multiple anyons coalesce. This work opens doors to understanding the macroscopic behavior of anyons, for which rich phases have been predicted theoretically.

items.title: Orbital Angular Momentum Currents and Textures in a Multiorbital Double Helix
items.summary: The microscopic origin of chirality induced spin selectivity (CISS) in biomolecular structures has traditionally been discussed in terms of spin orbit coupling and spin angular momentum. However, orbital angular momentum (OAM) is increasingly recognized as a more direct electronic response to molecular chirality. A helical hopping network built only from s orbitals can support an itinerant orbital moment and an orbital Edelstein response, but such a basis has no local atomic OAM and therefore omits the complementary contribution arising from coherence among active p orbitals. Here we construct a six-band multiorbital double helix model parameterized by characteristic B form DNA geometry and hopping scales. The model incorporates major minor groove asymmetry, an axial base pair offset representing stagger, and compositional inequivalence between the two strands, providing structural control parameters with which the orbital response can be tuned. Inter strand hybridization generates a full three component atomic OAM texture in the corotating local helical frame, including a radial component absent in the corresponding single helix model. We separately evaluate the itinerant OAM using the Bloch wave packet formulation of orbital magnetization and identify an additional inter-strand circulation channel unique to the double-helix connectivity. The resulting atomic and itinerant responses have distinct microscopic origins, magnitudes, and temperature dependences, establishing a multiorbital framework for geometry controlled angular momentum generation and transport in chiral molecular conductors.

items.title: Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.summary: Superconducting travelling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) provide broadband gain, low added noise, and high dynamic range, making them attractive for applications requiring wide instantaneous bandwidth. This is crucial for amplifying multiplexed narrow band signals spread over a wide frequency range, such as qubit resonator arrays, or amplifying inherently wide band signals, such as in spectrometers or radiometers. In many cases, however, the useful bandwidth of a TWPA is limited by the production of the idler tone at an image frequency. For three-wave-mixing (3WM) TWPAs, for example, an input signal at $f_s$ is indistinguishable from one at $f_p - f_s$, which can produce spectral ambiguity when the input spectrum is broadband or not known in advance. We experimentally demonstrate a balanced architecture that doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth available to a 3WM TWPA by spatially separating the amplified signal from the output pump and generated idler, which resolves the sideband degeneracy. The architecture consists of two amplifiers connected between a pair of 180$^{\circ}$ hybrid couplers, with the signal and pump injected and output through the sum and difference ports, respectively. Using two kinetic-inductance TWPAs, we demonstrate approximately 20 dB of signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, together with pump rejection below --20 dB and an average image rejection of approximately --15 dB over the operating band. These results establish balanced TWPAs as a practical approach to broadband parametric amplification, enabling improved contamination free bandwidth and eliminating the need for complex filtering.

items.title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
items.summary: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.

items.title: Exponential clustering of bipartite quantum entanglement at arbitrary temperatures
items.summary: Macroscopic quantum effects play central roles in the appearance of inexplicable phenomena in low-temperature quantum many-body physics. Such macroscopic quantumness is often evaluated using long-range entanglement, i.e., entanglement in the macroscopic length scale. The long-range entanglement not only characterizes the novel quantum phases but also serves as a critical resource for quantum computation. Thus, the problem that arises is under which conditions can the long-range entanglement be stable even at room temperatures. Here, we show that bi-partite long-range entanglement is unstable at arbitrary temperatures and exponentially decays with distance. Our theorem provides a no-go theorem on the existence of the long-range entanglement. The obtained results are consistent with the existing observations that long-range entanglement at non-zero temperatures can exist in topologically ordered phases, where tripartite correlations are dominant. In the derivation of our result, we introduce a quantum correlation defined by the convex roof of the standard correlation function. We establish an exponential clustering theorem for generic quantum many-body systems for such a quantum correlation at arbitrary temperatures, which yields our main result by relating quantum correlation to quantum entanglement. As a simple application of our analytical techniques, we derived a general limit on the Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information and the quantum Fisher information, which will attract significant attention in the field of quantum metrology. Our work reveals novel general aspects of low-temperature quantum physics and sheds light on the characterization of long-range entanglement.

items.title: Anti-synchronized collective rotation in magnetic colloidal particles under rotating magnetic fields
items.summary: Collective synchronization is a common response of interacting magnetic particles subjected to rotating external fields. Here we demonstrate a distinct nonequilibrium state in a two-dimensional cluster of magnetic colloidal particles in which the ordered crystalline core rotates, on average, opposite to the direction of the applied rotating magnetic field, while the defect-rich outer region continues to rotate with the drive. We term this state anti-synchronized collective rotation. By combining structural, spectral, bond-resolved, and layer-resolved torque analyses, we show that anti-synchronization is associated with a broader defect-rich interface, enhanced and dynamically heterogeneous bond deformation, and a reorganization of torque transmission between the surface and the crystalline interior. In the synchronized state, steric torques compensate the opposing dipolar contribution in the outer core, maintaining a positive net interaction torque. In the anti-synchronized state this compensation becomes insufficient, producing a negative net torque in theouter core and enabling core-surface rotational decoupling. Increasing the driving frequency restores coherent rotation through a transition characterized by competing positive- and negative-angular-velocity populations and hysteresis, consistent with a discontinuous, first-order-like dynamical transition. These results demonstrate how deformation and spatial redistribution of interaction torques can generate counter-rotating collective states in driven colloidal matter.

items.title: Sampling the XY model with an attention-based neural network
items.summary: We present a transformer-based variational autoregressive network for sampling lattice systems with continuous degrees of freedom and apply it to the two-dimensional XY model near the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. The architecture is combined with physics-informed ingredients: locality-informed attention and approximate probabilities. The resulting sampler significantly outperforms existing neural samplers. We train the model on lattices up to $96\times96$, verify with a mode-dropping estimator that no parts of the configuration space are missed, and reproduce the energy, magnetization and helicity modulus obtained with the traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm.

items.title: Transport and thermalization under noncommuting localized constraints
items.summary: We investigate the effects of spatially localized conserved quantities on transport and thermalization in quantum and classical many-body systems. We consider several related models: the integrable quantum Volterra model, its nonintegrable classical limit, and two cellular automata derived from the latter. Although localized constraints are often associated with lattice gauge theories, our models do not admit such an interpretation. In systems with discrete degrees of freedom, these constraints induce uniform fragmentation of the Hilbert or configuration space. In the quantum Volterra model, we derive an exact mapping of the dynamics within each Hilbert-space fragment onto a quantum chiral Potts chain. We find that energy transport is ballistic, with identical transport coefficients across all fragments. In the nonintegrable classical limit, energy transport is diffusive, and we similarly find the diffusion constant to be independent of whether or not the constraints are fixed (resolved). Finally, in the cellular automata, we show that, despite leaving transport unaffected, localized constraints lead to a strong breakdown of local ergodicity.

items.title: Mesoscopic learning dynamics of extensive-width neural networks
items.summary: Understanding how stochastic gradient descent learns internal representations in wide neural networks trained on rich target functions is a central problem in machine learning. We study this question in two-layer neural networks learning target functions represented by networks of the same architecture, with arbitrary nonlinearity, and with network width and input dimension growing proportionally. In this regime, standard approaches for describing the learning dynamics require tracking a diverging number of overlaps, which measure correlations between learned and target features, leaving no obvious description in terms of a few order parameters. Here, we develop a mesoscopic description of learning by characterizing the distribution of overlaps. In the early stages of learning, we find that a Gaussian description of overlap statistics reduces the learning dynamics to a few collective variables that track learning of the target function's linear and quadratic components. We then estimate the timescale of specialization, when Gaussian closure breaks down and individual learned features begin to strongly correlate with specific target features. We find that specialization in extensive-rank networks is accelerated via a quadratic shielding mechanism, whereby learning the linear and quadratic components of the target function filters gradient fluctuations. We finally describe how the activation function determines the pattern of specialization and characterize the subsequent refinement of learned features. Together, these results show how collective learning gives way to individual feature discovery and clarify when learning in large neural networks admits a simple statistical description.

items.title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
items.summary: Developing a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) that is accurate for the specific conditions under which it will be applied, rather than simply for the predefined configurations chosen by the model developer, is a significant challenge in atomistic simulation. Active learning (AL) addresses this challenge by closing the loop between candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating. Here, we survey more than seventy studies, with an emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, to understand how active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies. he reviewed examples include on-the-fly molecular dynamics, active data selection for fine-tuning pretrained models, kernel- and representation-based acquisition using frozen pretrained models, and reaction-aware sampling for chemical systems far from equilibrium. We explore the use of active learning in elemental and alloy mechanics, hydrogen and ion diffusion, ferroelectrics and effective Hamiltonians of functional materials, reactive and photochemical dynamics, high-entropy and compositionally disordered materials, as well as generative and autonomous material discovery pipelines. Drawing on a growing body of critical, methodologically self-aware literature, we also show that this achievement carries systematic caveats. Uncertainty estimates are not interchangeable across model architectures and are frequently the least reliable exactly where they matter most. We close by discussing the outlook for standardized, uncertainty-calibrated, and observable-targeted active-learning workflows in the foundation-model era.

items.title: Circuit-based characterization of finite-temperature quantum phases and self-correcting quantum memory
items.summary: Quantum phases at zero temperature can be characterized as equivalence classes under local unitary transformations: two ground states within a gapped phase can be transformed into each other via a local unitary circuit. We generalize this circuit-based characterization of phases to systems at finite-temperature thermal equilibrium described by Gibbs states. We construct a channel circuit that approximately transforms one Gibbs state into another provided the two are connected by a path in parameter space along which a certain correlation-decay condition holds. For finite-dimensional systems of linear size $L$ and approximation error $ε$, the locality of the circuit is ${\rm polylog}({\rm poly}(L)/ε)$. The correlation-decay condition, which we specify, is expected to be satisfied in the interior of many noncritical thermal phases, including those displaying discrete symmetry breaking and topological order. As an application, we show that any system in the same thermal phase as a zero-temperature topological code coherently preserves quantum information for a macroscopically long time, establishing self-correction as a universal property of thermal phases. As part of the proof, we provide explicit encoding and decoding channel circuits to encode information into, and decode it from, a system in thermal equilibrium.

items.title: Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity
items.summary: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering functionalities attractive for spintronics and quantum devices. Their practical use, however, is constrained by the limited availability of materials that simultaneously possess the required altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting electronic structure, and weak spin-orbit coupling. Here we show that these requirements can instead be separated between constituent materials through proximity engineering. We develop an analytical theory for a conventional semiconductor coupled to a gapped $d$-wave altermagnet and demonstrate that virtual tunneling transfers the altermagnetic spin splitting to the semiconductor. Crucially, the induced nonrelativistic and relativistic spin splittings exhibit qualitatively different dependences on band alignment. Virtual processes involving the valence and conduction bands of the altermagnet can reinforce the altermagnetic splitting while contributing with opposite signs to the interfacial Rashba coupling. Consequently, electrostatic tuning can access a regime in which the Rashba splitting vanishes while a sizable $d$-wave spin splitting persists. Exact diagonalization of the full heterostructure model confirms the analytical theory and establishes the robustness of this mechanism beyond the perturbative regime. Our results identify altermagnetic proximity as a route for engineering nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states in established semiconductor platforms, providing a general strategy for disentangling magnetic and relativistic spin interactions in quantum heterostructures.

items.title: Higher-Dimensional Information Lattice: Quantum State Characterization through Inclusion-Exclusion Local Information
items.summary: Developing a local description of quantum information is a central problem in quantum many-body physics: the goal is to identify how correlations are organized across positions and scales without choosing specific observables. We introduce a higher-dimensional information lattice, an inclusion-exclusion construction that decomposes the von Neumann information of reduced density matrices into contributions labeled by subsystem position and scale. Above one dimension, overlapping subsystems can form loops, allowing information associated with one subsystem to be inferred nonlocally from the density matrices of others. The sign of the inclusion-exclusion information resolves such overlap redundancies in position and scale: positive values mark positions and scales with net information gain, while negative values occur where redundant contributions dominate new ones. We implement the construction in two dimensions and apply it to many-body ground states with distinct entanglement structures. For localized states, such as disordered-localized states or gapped ground states of local Hamiltonians, the local information decays exponentially along different directions, defining direction-dependent information length scales. In critical states with a Fermi surface, decay becomes algebraic, with dominant directions tied to the velocity of gapless modes. In the toric code, topological order manifests as a negative information value at the largest lattice scale, interpreted as global information redundancy between the smallest loop-enclosing overlapping subsystems. We also isolate the universal information carried by edge states and locate the signatures of non-Abelian fusion channels in position and scale. Our results establish the higher-dimensional information lattice as a framework for resolving universal correlation structures through the spatial and scale distribution of quantum information.

items.title: Scaling of entanglement with distance between subsystems: detection of phase transitions in the $t'$-$π$-flux model
items.summary: The system-size scaling of bipartite entanglement can be used to detect phase transitions. We develop a related approach for strongly correlated electron models where large density matrices or large system size scaling are inaccessible. To this end, we demonstrate that phase transitions of various kinds are signaled by a sharp signature in the first- or second-order logarithmic derivatives of the negativity measuring entanglement between small clusters at varying distances. Crucially, we show how to mitigate the effect of quantum Monte Carlo noise at large distances when computing the negativity. Our focus is on the $t'$-$π$-flux Hubbard model using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations. It has the particular advantage of showing three distinct phase transitions in a single model: semimetal to band insulator, semimetal to antiferromagnetic Mott insulator, and a magnetic order-disorder transition belonging to the Gaussian, Gross-Neveu, and O(3) Wilson-Fisher universality classes, respectively.

items.title: Temperature and Thickness Dependent Spin Current Transmission through Epitaxial Antiferromagnetic α-Fe2O3
items.summary: Antiferromagnetic insulator α-Fe2O3 is a potential medium for coherent motion of spin waves over relatively large distances, allowing non-dissipative transfer of information between circuit elements. However, the structural defects and temperature dependent spin reorientations in this oxide impact the propagation. Understanding how the magnetic state of an antiferromagnetic insulator affects spin-current transmission is therefore important for elucidating the mechanisms governing spin transport. Here, we report spin-current transmission through epitaxial α-Fe2O3 thin films sandwiched between Permalloy and Pt. Using spin pumping and inverse spin Hall effect, we observe a finite symmetric dc voltage across the Pt layer over the temperature range 1.6 to 300 K for alpha-Fe2O3 thicknesses of 0, 30, 40, and 100 nm. The symmetric voltage coefficient Ks exhibits two approximately linear temperature regimes, separated by a characteristic temperature T* whose value depends on the thickness of the α-Fe2O3 layer. Further, the dc magnetization measurements on some of the samples suggest that the T* is correlated with the spin reorientation transition (Morin transition) in α-Fe2O3. Interestingly, a significantly larger magnitude of dKs/dT is noted below the characteristic temperature T*. The observed thickness and temperature dependent spin-current transmission indicates a sensitivity to the magnetic state of the insulating hematite layer.

items.title: Limits from nonlinear loss of spin-orbit-torque control of magnon transport
items.summary: Controlling magnon currents is central to the development of magnonic devices, which exploit spin excitations for information transport without charge flow. Here, we use the spin-orbit torque (SOT) from a Pt gate to control the effective magnon damping in three-terminal devices fabricated from low-damping lithium aluminum ferrite (LAFO) thin films and identify the nonlinear damping that ultimately limits the gate response. With increasing gate current, the nonlocal magnon signal initially increases, but saturates and subsequently decreases above a critical gate current density. Brillouin light scattering microscopy reveals that this turnover coincides with the emergence of an SOT-driven auto-oscillation mode localized beneath the gate, whose frequency continuously redshifts with increasing gate current, characteristic of large-amplitude nonlinear dynamics, and with a suppression of the propagating magnon population away from the gate. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the observed nonmonotonic gate response only when an amplitude-dependent effective damping is included, indicating that nonlinear losses, rather than saturation of spin injection, limit the degree of magnon modulation. Our results show that SOT compensation of magnon damping is ultimately limited by nonlinear damping attributed to auto-oscillations, providing a framework for understanding the limits of magnon current modulation in magnetic insulators.

items.title: Type 1.5 vortex bags in single component Ginzburg-Landau models with higher order potentials
items.summary: We demonstrate the existence of type 1.5 like superconductivity in a single component Ginzburg-Landau model with a higher order potential. The model exhibits two competing superconducting Meissner states (MS), each of which has its own pair of length scales (coherence length and penetration depth). The solutions take the form of bags that contain vortices of one vacuum inside the other. This gives rise to four different types of vortex interaction, where one set of length scales determines vortex interactions inside the bags and the other set between the bags. Hence, within the bag the vortices can repel or attract and the bags themselves can repel or attract depending on the hierarchy of four length scales. When vortices repel within the bag, solutions act similarly to those in type 1.5 multicomponent superconductors, but in a single component system.

items.title: Universality classes, Thermodynamics of Group Entropies, and Black Holes
items.summary: Conventional Boltzmann--Gibbs statistical mechanics successfully describes systems with weak to moderate correlations, in which the number of accessible configurations $W(N)$ grows exponentially with the number of degrees of freedom $N$. However, this framework breaks down for systems for which the effectively occupied configuration space exhibits non-exponential growth. While numerous generalized entropies have been proposed to address this limitation, a coherent link to classical thermodynamic laws has remained elusive. Here, we propose group entropies as a unifying framework, defining universality classes of entropies through the asymptotic scaling of $W(N)$, each yielding an extensive entropy. We show that this approach provides the basis for a consistent thermodynamic formulation beyond the Boltzmann--Gibbs paradigm. In particular, by expressing these entropies in terms of thermodynamic state variables, we demonstrate their consistency with classical thermodynamics, in close analogy to the emergence of the Clausius entropy from the Boltzmann--Gibbs formalism. Focusing on the zeroth thermodynamic law, we identify the empirical temperature and, by using Carathéodory's formulation of the second law, we derive the associated absolute temperature. As an application, we analyse black-hole thermodynamics using the extensive group entropy class corresponding to stretched-exponential behaviour of $W(N)$ and derive a negative heat capacity, known to be a hallmark property of black holes. This result holds for the stretched-exponential entropies associated with both the Bekenstein--Hawking and Barrow entropy scalings.

items.title: Analysis of Transient Microscopy Data in Reciprocal Space
items.summary: Transient microscopy has evolved to include a family of well-established techniques for studying the spatiotemporal dynamics of excited states in a variety of materials systems. In these methods, a laser pulse is focused to locally excite a material, and the subsequent evolution of the excited species is visualized to extract transport parameters such as diffusivities. Typically, transport coefficients are extracted from experimental datasets using curve-fitting methods to analyze the change in the mean squared displacement (MSD) of the spatial profiles over time. However, this approach can lead to inaccurate or misleading diffusivity values under many common experimental conditions, and is only formally accurate for the case of a single diffusing species. In this work, we introduce a new approach to the analysis of transient microscopy data based on the evolution of profile shapes in reciprocal space. We use simulated datasets to quantitatively analyze the performance of our proposed methods and compare them to current state-of-the-art analysis techniques. We demonstrate that reciprocal-space-based analysis methods have the highest overall performance in terms of accuracy and precision for normal diffusive transport over a range of realistic initial conditions and signal-to-noise ratios. Furthermore, we highlight the limitations of using MSD alone to characterize anomalous transport in materials, and we show how analysis of spatial frequencies can yield a more comprehensive understanding of complex excited-state dynamics and their underlying physical mechanisms. Our results show that reciprocal-space-based analysis methods are powerful tools for characterizing and quantifying many different types of transport behaviors.

items.title: Chiral Valence-Bond Solid and Chiral Triplons
items.summary: We propose a chiral valence-bond solid (VBS) in which spin-singlet bond order itself spontaneously acquires handedness without magnetic order. Using a spin-lattice model on the diamond lattice, we demonstrate two enantiomorphic VBS states. In the presence of anisotropic spin interactions, this emergent handedness is inherited by chiral triplons with spin-split bands and spin textures that reverse between the two enantiomers. These textures generate a temperature-gradient-induced net spin response whose sign is set by the VBS handedness. The imaginary off-diagonal components of the dynamical spin structure factor encode the triplon polarization and change sign between the two enantiomers, enabling direct detection of chiral triplons and the selected handedness by polarized inelastic neutron scattering. Our results establish a direct connection between spontaneous chirality and magnetic excitations, opening avenues for exploring the interplay between quantum magnetism and chiral physics.

items.title: Learning the self-energy through equivariant neural networks
items.summary: The electronic self-energy determines the single-particle Green's function and, through it, quasiparticle energies and spectral functions, but computing it from first principles is expensive and it is a difficult machine-learning target: complex-valued, matrix-valued in a local-orbital basis, and dependent on a continuous frequency. We predict the dynamical correlation part of the imaginary-frequency G_0W_0 self-energy matrix of molecules from atomic species and coordinates with an E(3)-equivariant message-passing network, the rotational covariance of the orbital-space matrix being imposed by the architecture itself and the static exchange part taken from the density-functional reference. Frequency enters either as an explicit network input or through frequency-specific output heads, and the predicted matrices are continued to the real axis in a representation in which causality and a non-negative spectral density hold by construction. The frequency-conditioned model reproduces matrix elements to below 1 meV on the imaginary axis for the systems studied here, and that accuracy survives the continuation: for water clusters, including a tetramer absent from the training set, and for chemically diverse molecules from QM9, the reconstructed spectral functions follow the G_0W_0 reference peak by peak and the frontier quasiparticle levels are recovered to a few tens of meV. Learning the self-energy on the imaginary axis is therefore a practical route to real-frequency spectra: once the model is trained, and given the density-functional reference it is built on, a new geometry costs no explicit G_0W_0 calculation.

items.title: In-Plane Differentiation and Out-of-Plane Coherence in Superconducting K$_{2-x}$Fe$_{4+y}$Se$_5$
items.summary: The structural link between superconductivity and anomalous $d_2$ diffraction signatures in K$_{2-x}$Fe$_{4+y}$Se$_5$ remains unresolved. Their appearance is accompanied by pronounced host-lattice evolution rather than a static structural background. Using high-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction, we show that excess Fe alters the vacancy-ordered host lattice, with structural differences between superconducting and nonsuperconducting states emerging before the $d_2$ features appear. All observed $d_2$ reflections can be described using two characteristic in-plane spacings and a nearly common low-temperature $c$ parameter. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal that superconductivity is associated with persistent in-plane differentiation and enhanced Fe-layer coherence along the $c$ axis. These results establish host-lattice evolution as the common structural origin linking the $d_2$ family and superconductivity, and suggest that the host-lattice differentiation identified here represents a structural analogue of the symmetry redistribution in FeSe.

items.title: Failure of the mean-field Hartree approximation for a bosonic many-body system with non-Hermitian Hamiltonian
items.summary: Mean-field Hartree theory is a central tool for reducing many-body dynamics to an effective one-particle evolution. This approximation has been employed when the Hamiltonian governing the many-body dynamics is not Hermitian. Indeed, non-Hermitian Hamiltonians model particle gain/loss or the evolution of open quantum systems between consecutive quantum jumps. Furthermore, the validity of the Hartree approximation for generic non-Hermitian Hamiltonians lies at the basis of a quantum algorithm for nonlinear differential equations. In this work, we show that this approximation can fail. First, we consider the most general bosonic mean-field Hamiltonian with two-body interactions and we prove that, for non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, the Hartree equation does not capture the correct second time derivative of the one-particle marginal state at $t=0$ in the thermodynamic limit. Then, we analytically solve a model of $N$ bosonic qubits with a purely anti-Hermitian Hamiltonian, compute the limit for $N\to\infty$ of the one-particle marginal state and show that it does not agree with the solution of the non-Hermitian Hartree equation. We further show that there exists an initial condition such that the exact one-particle marginal state undergoes a finite-time transition to a mixed state, a phenomenon that is completely absent in the case of Hermitian Hamiltonians. Finally, we simulate a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian with real spectrum and show that, also in this case, there are initial conditions for which the Hartree equation does not reproduce the correct one-particle marginal state in the limit $N\to\infty$. Our findings challenge the validity of the mean-field Hartree approximation for non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, and call for additional conditions for the validity of the mean-field regime to model the dynamics of particle gain and loss and the open-system dynamics in bosonic many-body systems.

items.title: Symmetry constraints on magnon-induced dynamics of skyrmion helicity in frustrated magnets
items.summary: The helicity of a magnetic skyrmion in a centrosymmetric frustrated magnet is a soft collective coordinate and a candidate variable for encoding quantum information. Its coherence is ultimately influenced by coupling to the magnon environment, which is commonly incorporated only phenomenologically. Here we combine a microscopic Keldysh treatment of the helicity--magnon coupling to resolve the contribution of individual magnon modes to the effective helicity dynamics. In the U(1)-symmetric model, the magnon bath generates, to leading order, a reactive helicity mass renormalization. When U(1) symmetry is broken, additional direct helicity--magnon couplings become allowed. In the presence of finite magnon lifetimes, these couplings generate an Ohmic contribution to the low-frequency helicity dynamics. The spatial symmetry of the perturbation determines which magnon sectors contribute to this damping, providing mode-resolved selection rules for the helicity--magnon coupling. Thus, we establish a microscopic connection between helicity dynamics and the excitation spectrum of frustrated skyrmions and identify the symmetry constraints governing dissipation of helicity-based quantum states.

items.title: Spatial and Temporal Control of Avalanches in Dense Active-Passive Mixtures
items.summary: Dense active--passive mixtures are often described within an effective-temperature picture, in which active dopants promote cage breaking and fluidize an arrested amorphous host. However, at sufficiently large persistence, the same dopants drive stress accumulation and localized void formation. Here we investigate the avalanche dynamics across this progression, focusing on the intermediate regime between dynamic arrest and void formation, where the system remains structurally homogeneous on average but relaxes through intermittent collective rearrangements rather than as a simple activated liquid. Using overdamped simulations of dilute active dopants embedded in a dense amorphous solid, we show that the avalanche dynamics separates into distinct spatial and temporal controls. For a given system size, the active fraction sets the size of the largest stress-release events, with a cutoff that grows as the square root of the fraction of dopants, $S_c\sim φ_a^{1/2}$, i.e., with the number of mean dopant spacings across the system, whereas persistence controls how avalanches unfold in time at fixed released stress. A decomposition of the stress into active and passive contributions, together with measurements of avalanche participation and morphology, shows that the active minority provides a localized and persistent driving channel while the surrounding amorphous packing carries the collective stress release. While the active minority controls the cutoff of the avalanche size statistics and the timing of the stress releases, the long-range elastic response and the building correlations in the passive host sets the size exponent, $τ_S\simeq1.1$, that is shared with externally sheared and uniformly active amorphous solids.

items.title: Finite-temperature phase diagram of dipolar bosons in a cylindrical setup
items.summary: Temperature plays a non-trivial role in dipolar systems, being able to either induce or destroy spatial density modulations. In order to shed light into the interplay between thermal effects and quantum correlations, we employ the path integral Monte Carlo method (PIMC) to obtain the phase diagram of a system of dipolar bosons in an infinite cylindrical geometry and at finite temperatures. For a fixed total density, we vary the scattering length of the interaction and the temperature, and characterize the structure and superfluidity of the emerging phases. The PIMC method accounts for thermal effects and quantum correlations at all orders, and can be used to quantitatively estimate the superfluid fraction of the system. Remarkably, we find a regime of parameters where, starting from a supersolid, the spatial order vanishes with temperature before the superfluidity does. We also find a region of the phase diagram where the superfluid fraction displays a non-monotonous dependence with temperature. Our results extend previous descriptions, relying on Bogoliubov theory, to larger temperatures in the thermodynamic limit and illustrate how spatial modulations and superfluidity are lost as temperature is increased.

items.title: Magnetic-field-free parity-protected qubit based on a narrow altermagnet Josephson junction
items.summary: Altermagnets provide a new route to engineer superconducting circuits without magnetic fields. We theoretically study the Andreev bound state (ABS) spectrum of a finite-width altrmagnet-based Josephson junction and show how the $d$-wave altermagnetic symmetry and geometric confinement shape its low-energy excitations. We find a clear distinction between the two $d$-wave symmetries: $d_{x^2-y^2}$ order produces spin splitting, whereas $d_{xy}$ order preserves spin degeneracy and exhibits splitting of the ABS spectrum induced by intermode hybridization. Leveraging these novel features, we propose applying a transverse electric field to tune the system and realize a magnetic-field-free, parity-protected superconducting qubit that we call altermon.

items.title: Plastic Flow Rule Based on Dislocation Link Velocity
items.summary: We develop a theory for the plastic shear rate $\dotγ_i$ on each slip system $i$ of face-centered cubic (FCC) single crystals, by integrating the shear rate contributions $\dotγ_i(l)$ from dislocation links of length $l$. A generalized Orowan equation expresses $\dotγ_i(l)$ in terms of the link density $n_i(l)$ and the average link velocity $v_i(l)$. This model accurately reproduces the discrete dislocation dynamics (DDD) shear-rate data for all 12 slip systems across 99 loading orientations. In particular, it explains why the plastic shear rate depends exponentially on the resolved shear stress $τ_i$, as reported previously, in the absence of any thermally activated mechanism. This dependence arises from the exponential tail of $n_i(l)$ filtered through the threshold-like velocity function $v_i(l)$. Furthermore, $v_i(l)$ is well approximated by a single two-dimensional function $v(τ_i,l)$ for all these slip systems. The link velocity is therefore governed mainly by $τ_i$ and $l$, with only a minor effect from the complex interactions between slip systems. These interactions instead manifest themselves mainly through $n_i(l)$. As a demonstration of the effect of the link-length distribution on the slip rate, we show that even when $τ_i$ is limited to a narrow window, the shear rates still span two orders of magnitude. The supply of long links is therefore the dominant factor controlling slip-system activity, outweighing the direct effect of $τ_i$ on the link velocity.

items.title: Fortuity and fragility in supersymmetric SYK
items.summary: In the $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric SYK model with $N$ fermions, every BPS state is fortuitous: at fixed charge, it exists only over a finite range of $N$. Allowing the charge to increase, we show that BPS classes may instead be uplifted along lattice walks inside the fortuity window, potentially to arbitrarily large $N$. However, there is no canonical uplift. We therefore introduce a decoder $D$ whose spectrum quantifies exact uplift and its metric cost. We call the failure or increasing cost of uplifting harmonic representatives metric fragility. Chen's single-matrix model and the protected tower of the two-flavor SYK model realize bare and genuinely dressed mechanisms of perfect uplift, respectively. In the generic one-flavor model, exact uplift eventually fails. The Lin-Maldacena-Rozenberg-Shan-type operator $D^\dagger D$ exhibits level statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble. Its eigenvalues quantify the metric continuity of BPS states across system size, while their correlations probe chaos within the BPS sector. Metric fragility and BPS chaos are thus encoded in complementary observables of the same operator, distinguishing chaotic BPS sectors from exactly solvable towers.

items.title: Scalable long-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling
items.summary: Accurate atomistic simulations of materials under electric fields require long-range electrostatics and electrical-response modeling at length scales beyond the reach of conventional first-principles methods. Yet these capabilities remain difficult to reconcile with the scalability of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Strictly local models enable efficient spatial parallelization but neglect long-range interactions, whereas existing electrostatic extensions introduce global dependencies that hinder distributed computation. Here, we overcome this limitation by analytically separating the long-range electrostatic forces and Born effective charges (BECs) into a global electrostatics calculation and strictly local derivatives of learned latent charges. This formulation preserves the spatial decomposability of equivariant MLIPs while enabling distributed evaluation of energies, forces, stresses, and BECs across different boundary conditions. Implemented as DPA4C-LR on the \texttt{nvalchemi} platform, the framework scales to 5.2 million atoms on four GPUs at approximately twice the computational cost of its short-range backbone. Trained on energies and forces, DPA4C-LR accurately infers BECs and reproduces the field-dependent infrared spectra of water. We further demonstrate its capabilities by recovering the characteristic slim polarization hysteresis of relaxor \ce{Pb(Mg_{1/3}Nb_{2/3})O3}, which is obscured by finite-size effects in smaller simulations; predicting a room-temperature field-driven ionic conductivity of $6.8 \pm 0.7$~mS/cm in amorphous \ce{Li_{0.9}NbO_{0.9}Cl_{4.1}}; and modeling interfacial thermal transport across Si/diamond interfaces with slab-corrected electrostatics. By combining long-range physics, electrical-response inference, and distributed computation, this framework extends predictive atomistic modeling toward device-relevant length scales.

items.title: Emergence of quantum transport in SnTe films upon structural refinement
items.summary: Topological crystalline insulators are distinguished from the conventional Z2 topological insulators by crystalline symmetry protection of the surface states. Quantitative characterization of these states requires magneto-transport measurements from which the phase coherence length and number of independent coherent channels can be extracted. Here we report such measurements on textured thin films of SnTe grown on Bi2Te3 buffered c-plane sapphire (Al2O3) by pulsed laser ablation. A post deposition annealing protocol was implemented to control the crystallographic texture, which reveals improved crystallinity and enhanced epitaxial alignment along the [111] direction in films annealed at elevated temperatures. The higher carrier density and lower resistivity seen in films annealed at 100 oC are suggestive of Sn vacancies which act as native acceptor defects, while films annealed at 200 oC approach the 1:1 stoichiometry. The magnetoresistance of all samples at T 20 K, the MR is small and positive, and deviates from conventional Kohler scaling. An approximate collapse of the MR curves between 50 and 250 K is obtained using an empirical temperature-dependent scaling factor, indicating that changes in the Hall-derived carrier density alone cannot account for the observed scaling behavior. These results demonstrate that post growth annealing strongly influences the interplay between stoichiometry, crystallinity, and coherent transport in SnTe thin films.

items.title: Grain boundary strength and corrosion cracking susceptibility in TiN coatings under fission product segregation
items.summary: During fuel-cladding chemical interaction (FCCI), lanthanide fission products generated in the fuel can migrate into cladding grain boundaries (GBs), where segregation may reduce GB strength and promote corrosion cracking. We use first-principles segregation, decohesion, and bonding calculations to quantify Nd and Ce effects on six coincident-site lattice GBs in bcc Fe and TiN. For each material, segregation energies, work-of-separation values for complete interfacial cleavage, and traction-separation curves measuring ideal resistance to crack opening were evaluated within a consistent computational framework. Nd and Ce segregate favorably to both materials, and the median segregation energies are more negative in TiN, showing that TiN does not simply exclude these species from internal interfaces. The mechanical responses of Fe and TiN differ sharply. In Fe, Nd and Ce consistently reduce work of separation and peak traction, with median work-of-separation retentions of 0.72 and 0.65 and median peak-traction retentions of 0.47 and 0.43. In TiN, most decorated GBs preserve much of the clean response, with median work-of-separation retentions of 1.00 and 0.97 and median peak-traction retention of 0.85 for both fission products. Bonding analysis shows weak, occupied antibonding X-Fe replacement bonds in Fe, whereas the surrounding Ti-N network remains largely preserved after Nd/Ce segregation in TiN. These results provide atomistic support for the use of TiN and related nitride coatings to reduce FCCI damage by retaining GB strength if fission products segregate to coating internal interfaces. This retention of GB strength also provides a mechanistic descriptor for assessing coating susceptibility to FCCI-assisted corrosion cracking and environmentally assisted intergranular fracture.

items.title: A Monte Carlo Study of the Dipolar Universality Class in Three Dimensions
items.summary: The dipolar universality class describes the phase transition in 3D ferromagnets with strong dipolar interactions, as first discussed by Aharony and Fisher in the 1970s.
