items.title: Inducing Extraordinary-log Criticality through a Quantum Spin Chain
items.summary: We demonstrate the emergence of extraordinary-log criticality in a quantum many-body system by coupling a spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg chain to a two-dimensional quantum critical Heisenberg bilayer. Under the quantum-to-classical mapping, the chain acts as a plane defect in a three-dimensional critical environment for which the extraordinary-log universality class has recently been predicted. Using large-scale sign-problem-free quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we directly probe the renormalization-group flow of the effective defect coupling through the spin stiffness. We observe the characteristic logarithmic growth with linear system size $L$, corresponding to a stable weak-coupling fixed point and a running coupling $g(L)\sim 1/\log L$. Furthermore, the extracted step-scaling function quantitatively follows the universal renormalization-group flow predicted for the extraordinary-log universality class, including the leading and subleading universal coefficients. Our results establish extraordinary-log criticality in a genuine quantum many-body setting and show that its universal behavior persists despite the topological $θ$-term present in the low-energy field theory of the isolated spin chain.

items.title: Emergence of Correlations Between Records and Maximum in Random Time Series
items.summary: We compute exactly the covariance between the maximum $M$ and the number of records $K$ in a discrete time series of $n$ entries as a quantitative probe of the history leading to an extreme event. For continuous IID series, with a common probability distribution function (PDF) $p(x)$, we find the striking result that $M$ and $K$ are uncorrelated for any $n \geq 1$. We show that this independence is rather fragile and the covariance $C_q(n)$ between $M$ and $K$ becomes nonzero when $p(x)$ becomes discontinuous due to a delta-component at $x=0$ with an amplitude $0 q_c$). We compute the critical strength $q_c$ exactly. Furthermore, for large $n$, we show that $C_q(n)$ decays as a power law, with an exponent that depends on the tail of $p(x)$. We then compare our theoretical predictions with real precipitation data from several weather stations across Germany, finding a very good agreement.

items.title: Fractionalized Fermi Liquid and d-wave Superconductivity in Ba2CuO3+x
items.summary: Strongly enhanced superconductivity (SC) (Tc = 73 K) in Ba2CuO3+x (BCO) challenges the longheld paradigm of the irrelevance of the dz2-like states in cuprates. Using tight-binding band structure plus dynamical mean-field theory (TB+DMFT), we find that a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FFL) is the normal state for the parameters realistic for BCO. Transport properties exhibit strange metal behavior above Tcoh~38 K, supporting a direct instability of this strange metal to SC. Irrelevance of one-fermion inter-band mixing, itself a non-trivial consequence of the FFL state, preferentially enhances two-fermion hopping processes and provides a novel route for both SC and competing excitonic order(s) arising directly from the FFL. The proposed scenario also clarifies the role of dz2 band in shaping the physical responses of BCO.

items.title: Non-Adiabatic Spin-Induced Currents in Magnetic Weyl Semimetals
items.summary: We theoretically study dc electric currents induced by rapid spin precession in noncentrosymmetric magnetic Weyl semimetals using the Floquet--Keldysh Green's-function formalism. The spin dynamics act as a time-dependent chiral gauge field and the geometric structure of electric currents is expressed in terms of the Berry curvature, the quantum metric, and the shift vector. For an isotropic Weyl cone, only an injection current is generated. This current scales quadratically with the driving frequency and linearly with the relaxation time associated with coupling to a fermionic bath. We further show that a finite Weyl-cone tilt modifies the available interband-transition phase space, smooths the frequency dependence of the current, and allows for a shift current and another type of injection current, both of which flow in directions determined by the tilt and the direction of the precession. A finite net current can remain after summing contributions from Weyl nodes of opposite chiralities when their transition phase spaces are inequivalent.

items.title: Period-dependent suppression of Fourier peaks for topography images: Analysis of periodicity of triple-step arrays on vicinal Si(h h m) surfaces
items.summary: Reliable determination of the periodicity of multiatomic steps on high-Miller-index vicinal surfaces is often complicated by (i) the presence of relatively narrow terraces tilted at large angles relative to the scanning plane, and (ii) unavoidable distortions in the lateral direction resulting from creep and improper calibration of a piezo scanner. This work paves a way to overcome these obstacles using the period-dependent Fourier peaks suppression, which is invariant to affine distortions of the atomically resolved scanning probe microscopy images and to defects of the terrace atomic structure. We argue that the period of the triple-step arrays fabricated on vicinal Si(5 5 6) and Si(5 5 7) single-crystal wafers can be determined from raw scanning tunneling microscopy data, without preliminary corrections, with precision approaching the interatomic distance. We demonstrate that the intensities of the Fourier peaks in the differential maps, derived from raw topography images and containing stripes with the $7\times7$ reconstruction, strongly depend on the period of the stripes. The suppression of the ninth Fourier peak indicates that the regular array of triple steps formed on the Si(5 5 7) wafers has a period of $18b=5.99$ nm in projection onto the Si(1 1 1) terrace plane, where $b=0.333$ nm is the distance between atomic rows of the $1\times 1$ lattice in the $[\bar{1} \bar{1} 2]$ direction. This means that the nominally (5\,5\,7)-oriented Si wafers may correspond locally to the Si(8 8 11) orientation. The method can be applied to the precise analysis of other vicinal surfaces with narrow and wide terraces containing an integer number of Si(1 1 1)$7\times7$ unit cells.

items.title: Multiple Superconducting Phases under Pressure for Different Field Directions in UTe2
items.summary: The existence of multiple superconducting phases is a striking feature of UTe2, arising from the spin and orbital degrees of freedom and supporting a spin-triplet superconducting state. We present field-temperature phase diagrams under pressure for fields applied along the three principal crystallographic axes, as determined by AC calorimetry measurements. The pressure evolution of the multiple superconducting phases is highly anisotropic with respect to magnetic field direction, revealing rich superconducting phenomena arising from complex fluctuations.

items.title: Universal Long-distance Tail of Particle-number Density near a Wall in Superfluids
items.summary: We investigate the long-distance recovery of the particle-number density near a static, impermeable wall in a $d$-dimensional Galilean-invariant superfluid. Using superfluid effective field theory (EFT) on a half-space, we show that quantum phonon fluctuations produce a $z^{-(d+1)}$ tail in the smooth density profile at zero temperature, where $z$ is the distance from the wall. The tail coefficient is fixed by the bulk equation of state and is independent of microscopic wall details. At low temperature $T$, the thermal length $c_s/T$, with $c_s$ the bulk sound speed, separates the zero-temperature behavior at intermediate distances from a thermal $Tz^{-d}$ tail at larger distances for $d>1$. For $d=1$, the long-distance phonon contribution instead decays as $\exp(-4πTz/c_s)$. The EFT applies to both Bose and Fermi superfluids, including strongly interacting Fermi gases at unitarity. We estimate the normalized tail amplitude in three dimensions across the BCS--BEC crossover using experimental sound-speed data.

items.title: Thermal Conductivity and Temperature-Induced Band Gap Renormalization in Crystalline and Amorphous Ga$_2$O$_3$
items.summary: The lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) and electron-phonon interactions in crystalline and amorphous gallium oxide are herein determined by coupling a machine-learned interatomic potential, namely the moment tensor potential (MTP) model, to first-principles calculations. Crystalline $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ exhibits a substantial band gap renormalization (BGR) of $\sim$0.45 eV at 700 K, with $\sim$0.2 eV caused by zero-point BGR. The computed temperature dependence of BGR induced by classical nuclear motion in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is stronger than that in amorphous Ga$_2$O$_3$, with the difference in BGR reaching $\sim$0.18 eV at 900 K. Thermal transport calculations reveal that the LTC of amorphous Ga$_2$O$_3$ remains near $0.9$ W$\cdot$ m$^{-1}$$\cdot$K$^{-1}$ for temperatures between 300 K and 700 K, which is approximately an order of magnitude lower than that of crystalline $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$. Overall, the presented framework provides a computationally tractable and reliable route for predicting properties of semiconductors (both crystalline and amorphous) under operating conditions relevant to microelectronics and optoelectronics.

items.title: Self-propulsion protocols for swift non-equilibrium state transitions and enhanced cooling in active systems
items.summary: A control framework is proposed for inducing non-equilibrium state transitions in confined active matter, where the statistics of self-propulsion serve as the only control parameter. Positivity of the noise amplitudes and fundamental bounds on position-propulsion correlations define the admissible control space and impose speed-limits on transitions between non-equilibrium states. We show that non-stationary initial states facilitate additional speed-ups, corresponding to pre-loading the state with negative correlations. This enables active cooling protocols that outperform their passive counterparts.

items.title: Confinement-induced toughening in delignified wood-polyacrylamide composite hydrogels
items.summary: With growing interest in environmental conservation, polymer composites incorporating wood-derived materials have attracted significant attention. While research has focused extensively on hard composites utilizing delignified wood or cellulose nanofibers (CNF) and soft composites reinforced with CNF, there have been a limited number of studies on the development of soft composites that utilize the porous cellular structure of wood, with few exceptions. In this study, we fabricated soft composites by infiltrating delignified wood with polyacrylamide hydrogel and subjected them to uniaxial compression tests. The results demonstrated that these materials exhibited far superior strength and toughness compared to either delignified wood or polyacrylamide hydrogel alone. Through systematic investigation and theoretical analysis, we identified the mechanisms underlying these enhancements in strength and toughness. Specifically, in addition to the sacrificial bond breakage known to enhance toughness in double-network hydrogels, we propose that mechanical confinement, arising from the soft, incompressible hydrogel filling the hollow cell lumens, generates excess stress and acts to resist compressive deformation. This approach, which utilizes the cellular structure as a filler, suggests the potential for creating a new class of high-toughness composite materials.

items.title: D-instanton Effects on the Holographic Weyl Semimetals
items.summary: We investigate the effects of D-instantons on a holographic Weyl semimetal in a top-down approach. We find that the presence of D-instantons induces a novel phase transition from a Weyl semimetal to a gapped phase, providing a new mechanism for gap formation in strongly coupled systems. By analyzing the free energy of probe D7-brane embeddings, we construct the phase diagram in terms of the fermion mass, instanton density, and temperature, measured in units of the Weyl parameter. We show that, in addition to the conventional mass-driven transition associated with band inversion, the instanton density gives rise to a qualitatively different transition whose mechanism cannot be understood within the standard Dirac picture. We compute nonlinear electric conductivities from the regularity condition at the black hole horizon and demonstrate that the two types of transitions exhibit distinct transport behavior. In particular, the instanton-induced transition leads to a gapped phase with properties that differ from the conventional insulating phase. We also discuss possible interpretations of this phase in the boundary theory and comment on its relation to nonperturbative effects in strongly interacting systems.

items.title: Light-induced local control of magnetic anisotropy and domain pattern in Co/Pt multilayers
items.summary: Control of magnetic anisotropy is essential for the fabrication of next-generation devices in spintronics and magnetic memory. While conventional approaches such as material composition, thermal annealing, and ion bombardment are widely used, achieving spatially resolved, continuous control remains a challenge. Herein, we demonstrate a dual-regime, localized control over both transient magnetic states and permanent intrinsic properties in perpendicularly magnetized Co/Pt multilayers using ultra-short laser pulses. By employing a multi-scale approach combining Kerr microscopy, magnetic force microscopy, and vibrating sample magnetometry, we reveal that low-fluence irradiation enables a reversible, helicity-dependent accumulation of magnetic phases without altering the intrinsic quasistatic properties. Conversely, high-fluence exposure acts as localized thermal annealing that permanently hardens the magnetic system. This structural relaxation leads to a substantial enhancement of the effective perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, driving a twofold increase in the local coercive field and expanding the equilibrium stripe domain width. By offering both reversible spin manipulation and deterministic engineering of 2D magnetic landscapes, this work paves the way towards flexible, lithography-free anisotropy structuring for advanced spintronic applications.

items.title: Field-induced incommensurate--commensurate transitions in anisotropic magnets
items.summary: We study field-induced incommensurate--commensurate transitions (ICTs) in classical spin chains with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) $D$, strong easy-plane anisotropy, and weak easy-axis anisotropy $A$ within the easy plane. This model describes systems with ferromagnetic layers coupled by exchange interaction with DMI. The magnetic field $\bf H$ is applied in the easy plane at an arbitrary angle $δ$ to the easy axis stabilizing a soliton lattice in the ground state. We consider ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic in-chain exchange interactions within the continuum limit and show that the easy-axis anisotropy leads to qualitatively different effects in these two cases: the ferromagnetic chain is described by a double-sine-Gordon-type equation with phase-shifted harmonics, whereas the antiferromagnetic chain reduces to a sine-Gordon equation. For the latter case, phase boundaries between incommensurate and commensurate states are found analytically in $(H,A,D,δ)$ space and confirmed by numerical calculations for certain $D$ and $δ$ values. Close to all ICTs, results of the continuum consideration become invalid due to a stochastic destruction of near-separatrix solutions which either make an ICT a first-order transition or stabilize states with spatially irregular soliton and antisoliton arrangements.

items.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
items.summary: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential field-induced phase transition into a collective electronic state driven by enhanced electron-electron interactions. Our findings provide valuable insights into the unconventional chiral transport and emergent correlated quantum states under extreme magnetic fields.

items.title: From quantum emitters to technological platforms: a perspective on semiconductor quantum dots
items.summary: Photonic quantum technologies are based on controlled photon states. To generate these, quantum dots have emerged as excellent sources of single and entangled photons. In this Perspective, we briefly review the chronological development of quantum dots as photon sources, from their beginnings as quantum emitters in the early 2000s to the advanced photonic devices being developed today. We highlight the interplay between fundamental research and industrial aspects before discussing the photonic quantum technologies we expect to emerge in the near future.

items.title: Nonergodicity from Hilbert-Subspace Cloning
items.summary: We identify a class of nonintegrable quantum many-body systems composed of single Pauli strings that possess an extensive number of noncommuting local conserved quantities and exhibit partial ergodicity breaking due to exponentially degenerate energy spectra. We show that such systems exhibit a novel mechanism, Hilbert-subspace cloning, where the identical chaotic Hamiltonian acts on each of exponentially many disconnected Hilbert subspaces. Although the dynamics within each clone thermalizes, quantum coherence between clones remains protected and detectable by local observables. Consequently, the long-time behavior of local observables is described by a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs ensemble, where the hidden subsystem retains its initial quantum coherence.

items.title: Fully gapped superconductivity in magic-angle graphene Cooper-pair islands
items.summary: The mechanism behind superconductivity in magic-angle graphene systems remains an open question. Recent tunnelling and superfluid stiffness measurements have suggested a nodal superconducting gap, but these probes are typically applied to large-area devices, where twist-angle inhomogeneity and disorder can hinder resolving the intrinsic superconducting spectrum. Here we introduce quantum dots in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and access a regime where gate-tunable superconductivity competes with strong Coulomb repulsion upon adding an additional carrier to the island. The islands exhibit $2e$-periodic Coulomb blockade, revealing a well-defined quasiparticle gap in the island spectrum, inconsistent with the presence of nodes in the order parameter. Within the same device, we also realize coupled superconducting islands and proximitized quantum dots, establishing a monolithic platform for hybrid dot devices. Our results point to a nodeless quasiparticle gap in moiré graphene and demonstrate the potential of mesoscopic hybrid structures to probe their correlated phases.

items.title: Discrete time crystals and classical logic gates in coupled open Dicke models
items.summary: We investigate the dynamics of coupled discrete time crystals (DTCs) in the coupled Dicke model or Dicke dimer (DD) with dissipation. By numerically simulating the mean-field dynamics of the system, we show that coupling two DTCs decreases their oscillation amplitude following a transient relaxation period. For sufficiently strong coupling, the coupled DTCs become unstable, resulting in the system relaxing towards the normal phase (NP). We demonstrate that the relaxation time diverges near the critical coupling strength, suggesting a continuous phase transition. Using the truncated Wigner approximation (TWA), we explore how the dynamics are affected by the introduction of quantum fluctuations. We also consider a scenario in which an NP is briefly coupled to a DTC, seeding the NP to transform into a DTC that is either synchronized or anti-synchronized relative to the DTC. We investigate the robustness of this phenomenon in the presence of noise. Using these results, we propose a scheme to perform NAND and NOR operations with three DTCs by sequentially coupling the input and output sites. We identify the parameter regimes in which the logic gate architecture remains valid, and investigate how the protocol is affected by the presence of quantum fluctuations.

items.title: Diffusion-controlled reactions with time-dependent surface reactivity
items.summary: We investigate diffusion-controlled reactions on a reactive surface with time-dependent reactivity. Starting from a conventional formulation via diffusion equation with Robin boundary condition for the macroscopic concentration of particles, we aim at quantifying how temporal variations of reactivity affect the survival probability and the associated first-reaction time (FRT) of a single particle on the reactive surface. Using an adiabatic description, we first identify five long-time regimes of the first-reaction time distribution, ranging from exponential and stretched-exponential to power-law decay. In particular, sufficiently rapid decay of the reactivity leads to a nonzero probability of never reacting, despite diffusion in a bounded domain. Second, we provide a probabilistic reformulation of this problem and compare it with a different scenario of encounter-dependent reactivity. Our theoretical predictions are validated via extensive Monte Carlo simulations.

items.title: Crystal Field-Phonon Coupling in ErFeO$_3$ Single Crystal Via Inelastic Neutron Scattering
items.summary: Crystal-field (CF) excitations and their coupling to lattice vibrations were investigated in ErFeO$_3$ using inelastic neutron scattering. Pronounced modifications of the excitation spectra, including energy shifts, intensity redistribution, and linewidth changes, were observed as a consequence of CF-phonon coupling. Significant renormalization of the first and second CF excitations, located near 5 meV and 12 meV, respectively, was detected along both transverse and longitudinal directions in the vicinity of the reciprocal-space point Q = (2, 0, 4). The coupling effects become more prominent as the temperature increases from 300 K to 650 K, while a slight suppression is observed at 750 K. Remarkably, CF excitation peaks that are strongly weakened by thermal population effects re-emerge in specific momentum regions through interaction with phonon modes. The coupled excitations exhibit characteristic signatures of hybridization, including energy renormalization, intensity enhancement, and linewidth narrowing. Density-functional-theory-based phonon calculations further support the interpretation of CF-phonon coupling in ErFeO3. These results demonstrate that strong interactions between CF excitations and lattice vibrations can substantially modify the excitation spectra in rare-earth orthoferrites.

items.title: Transport Signatures of a Kinetically Self-Trapped Nagaoka Polaron
items.summary: Nagaoka polarons are canonical examples of kinetic magnetism. Although their spin structure is well understood, their transport remains unexplored. We compute the dynamical mobility of a single hole in the square-lattice $t$-model using resummation-based quantum Monte Carlo and analytic continuation. Upon cooling, an incoherent Drude-like response gives way to a finite-frequency peak as the dc mobility vanishes. The peak signals an internal mode of a hole confined by its ferromagnetic cloud. Our results establish transport as an incisive probe of polaron formation and kinetic self-trapping.

items.title: Compact Fully Integrated Alignment-Free and Linearly Polarized Ho$^{3+}$ Single-Frequency Waveguide Laser
items.summary: We report, for the first time, a fully integrated Ho$^{3+}$-doped fluoride glass waveguide laser incorporating a femtosecond laser-inscribed waveguide and waveguide Bragg grating. A line-by-line inscription technique was employed to fabricate the Bragg gratings, yielding highly consistent and reproducible grating characteristics with precise control of the Bragg resonance wavelength. A compact 12.4 mm cavity achieves stable single-frequency lasing at 2062.21 nm with a linewidth of less than 5 MHz. The laser exhibits intrinsically linearly polarized emission. This alignment-free architecture provides a compact and robust platform for integrated mid-infrared single-frequency laser sources.

items.title: Emergent flocking dynamics in chemorepulsive active colloids: Interplay of disorder and noise
items.summary: Recent studies of active colloidal matter have revealed that a global polar order can arise from chemorepulsive interactions among particles without any explicit alignment interaction between them. In this work, we investigate such chemically interacting active colloids in the presence of quenched disorder, where a fraction of particles are randomly pinned in space. These pinned particles are restricted to rotational motion while remaining chemically coupled to the mobile population. In addition, angular noise is incorporated into the rotational dynamics to capture stochastic effects. To elucidate the interplay of quenched disorder and noise, we construct phase diagrams based on polar order and its fluctuations, and systematically analyze the associated disorder- and noise-driven phase transitions. Surprisingly, we find that the phase transition driven by the noise is significantly dependent on the density of the particles, whereas such a density-dependence is not present when the control parameter is the pinning fraction. The finite-size effects on these transitions are also examined. We demonstrate that an effective interaction range, governed by the coefficient related to the screening of the chemorepulsive interaction, plays a crucial role in collective behavior. When the effective interaction range is much smaller than the system size, the system exhibits density band formation, a feature absent in the long-range interaction regime. Moreover, near the transition point, the order parameter distribution becomes bimodal for the case of short-range interaction.

items.title: Parity-dependent sublattice structure of local $2\times2$ correlations in domino tilings of the Aztec diamond
items.summary: We study local $2\times2$ correlations in uniformly random domino tilings of the Aztec diamond $\mathrm{AZ}(n)$, a dimer model with frozen corners and a liquid region bounded by the Arctic circle, and compare them with the square chessboard. For every elementary square the probabilities $P_H$ and $P_V$ of the two coverings by a pair of parallel dominoes satisfy $P_H=P_V=P_1P_2+P_3P_4$, where $P_1,\dots,P_4$ are the probabilities of the four surrounding edges. This known identity, a case of Kuo's graphical condensation, reduces the spatial profile of $P_H$ to single-edge probabilities, which we compute exactly from the inverse Kasteleyn matrix for all squares of $\mathrm{AZ}(n)$. The squares form two interleaved sublattices, distinguished by the color of their lower-left cell. The parity of $n$ decides which sublattice dominates near the center: the one containing the central square for odd $n$, and the other one for even $n$. This sign rule holds for the averaged sublattice contrast for all $4\le n\le22$. It also fixes the location of the global maximum of $P_H$, which lies at or next to the center for odd $n$ and several lattice spacings away for even $n$. Within the central sublattice, the preferred square follows a mod-4 pattern that matches the exactly pinned mean height of the center. On the $L\times L$ chessboard the same rule holds with $n$ replaced by the half-width $L/2$, but the contrast is two to six times weaker, the central edge probability never equals $1/4$, and the maxima of $P_H$ are pinned to the corners. The exact $1/4$ values and the interior, parity-selected maxima are therefore features of the Aztec geometry.

items.title: Spectral theory of energy-selective quantum search with Ising Hamiltonian phase oracles
items.summary: We develop an exact spectral-response theory for the Grover-type iterate \(W_T=D_ξ\exp(-\mathrm{i} T H)\), in which the evolution generated by a diagonal Ising Hamiltonian is used directly as a continuous phase oracle. An energy-grouped recurrence and its generating-function solution show how the empirical characteristic function determines the position, width, height, and saturation time of an energy-selective resonance. For an annealed Gaussian density of states, a high-density-tail resonance containing \(M\) configurations is reached after \(Θ(\sqrt{2^n/M})\) oracle calls with success probability \(Θ(1)\), giving a quadratic query improvement over independent uniform sampling with classical energy evaluation. For correlated random Ising spectra, overlap-dependent covariances lead to a realization-dependent resonance shift with root-mean-square scale \(O(n^{-3})\), parametrically larger than the resonance width, and can also reduce the peak height. The shift is both an algorithmic detuning and a coherent probe of sample-specific spectral fluctuations whose ensemble statistics reflect the Ising overlap structure. Spectral symmetrization and iterative calibration can remove or compensate the resonance-center displacement for prescribed-energy targeting. We also clarify the relation to designed spectral filters and the precision and coherence requirements of this asymptotic primitive.

items.title: Kitaev, semi-Dirac, and spinon quantum spin Hall liquids on the square-hexagon-dodecagon lattice: A parent projective symmetry group classification
items.summary: The square-hexagon-dodecagon (SHD) lattice hosts an exactly solvable Kitaev spin liquid, while further-neighbor couplings frustrate its Heisenberg magnet into classically degenerate lines where quantum fluctuations can melt the Néel order. To place this state among the lattice's spin liquids, we classify fermionic parton mean-field states with singlet and spin-orbit-coupled triplet amplitudes by their projective symmetry groups (PSGs). As SHD sites lack site symmetry, its $Z_2$ PSGs are the projective classes of $p6mm$ with time reversal, from which those of every single-orbit $p6mm$ lattice follow. In the idealized Kitaev model, where lattice operations do not rotate spins, these liquids carry a single $Z_2$ PSG descending from the $SU(2)$ Lieb-flux state, and their projections are exact eigenstates. The PSG's sixfold-rotation sign, fixed by the dodecagon flux, doubles all Majorana bands, and the mirrors exclude a chiral phase in any uniform field, so only a sublattice-staggered three-spin term drives the non-Abelian Ising phase. Beyond the Kitaev state, we find a critical semi-Dirac spin liquid, with mean-field correlations $\propto r^{-3}$ along three directions and $r^{-6}$ otherwise, and extended Dirac phases with up to $48$ fermion flavors, among them an $N_f=12$ state whose PSG forbids every singlet mass. Out-of-plane Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya couplings gap the Dirac states of its $U(1)$ class into a mean-field spinon counterpart of the Kane-Mele quantum spin Hall insulator, with spin Chern number $1$ or $3$ and spin-carrying monopoles. Chiral states imply Kalmeyer-Laughlin, semion$\times$semion, and three-fermion orders, rotation-breaking ones show $q\to -q$ asymmetric neutron spectra, and sign-alternating fluxes break time reversal alone. Masses and monopoles in these many-flavor phases and the energetics of frustrated SHD Heisenberg models are natural next steps.

items.title: Residual diagnostics for detecting the breakdown of the single power-law approximation in photoelectron yield spectroscopy: application to doped silicon
items.summary: Our automated analysis of photoelectron yield spectroscopy (PYS) estimates the threshold Ith and the exponent n of a single power law for every spectrum. When this model fits poorly, however, the analysis cannot tell whether the data or the model is at fault. Here we present residual diagnostics that separate the two causes. The exponent is scanned continuously on a 1/n-power fit with an Akaike information criterion (AIC) based on the mean absolute error (MAE), and the spread of the resulting Akaike weights ($P \times Δn$) quantifies the uncertainty of the estimate. The normalized MAE (NMAE) and the RMSE-to-MAE ratio (RMR) assess the data quality, the Durbin-Watson (DW) statistic assesses the model adequacy, and the three checks are reported in parallel. With criteria set from an Au reference, the diagnostics were applied to 60 continuous measurements in air of four HF-treated Si samples. For heavily doped p-type Si, DW fell below its criterion, whereas the means of NMAE and RMR remained within their criteria. Prompted by this flag, we fitted the spectrum with a two-component model with fixed exponents (n = 1 and 2.5); the AIC decreased by 56, DW increased from 0.86 to 1.99, and the two components set in at 4.70 and 5.28 eV. For heavily doped n-type Si, the change during air exposure was consistent with a single component. The diagnostics thus identify the spectra that require a multi-component analysis without assuming an emission mechanism.

items.title: Wetting by active fluids
items.summary: The Young-Dupré equation is a cornerstone of the theory of capillary and wetting phenomena that governs the shape of droplets adsorbed on surfaces in equilibrium. But many living and synthetic materials, such as swarming bacteria and active colloids, are composed of self-propelled particles that are inherently out of thermal equilibrium. The description of the wetting of surfaces by such active fluids thus requires a new framework. Here, we develop an analogue to the Young-Dupré equation for systems made of self-propelled particles. A key step is to define the liquid-gas surface tension of active fluids as the force exerted along the interface, which we show from first principles to be negative, even when active materials separate into stable liquid and gas phases. The active Young-Dupré equation explains why partial wetting appears in simulations where the surface tensions do not balance and reveals the underlying feedback mechanism: the interface is stable only because of steady flows, which are themselves generated by the parity-symmetry-breaking interface. Unlike in passive fluids, where the droplets are scale-free, this feedback loop selects the sizes and shapes of adsorbed droplets in active materials. Our results outline a framework for understanding how active matter wets surfaces.

items.title: Hidden Staggered Superconducting Order in V2Se2O-Family Altermagnets
items.summary: $η$ pairing describes a staggered superconducting condensate whose order parameter changes sign between neighboring unit cells while maintaining a uniform magnitude. Nearly four decades after its theoretical proposal by C. N. Yang, a material platform for stabilizing $η$ pairing has remained elusive. Here, we reveal that altermagnetism, despite being pair breaking for conventional BCS pairing, naturally favors $η$-like pairing in V$_2$Se$_2$O-family altermagnets. Their valley-contrasting spin structure gives rise to oppositely spin-polarized, symmetry-related valleys centered at $X=(π,0)$ and $Y=(0,π)$, which form spin-singlet pairing partners separated by the commensurate momentum $\mathbf Q=(π,π)$, thereby favoring an $η$-like condensate. Self-consistent calculations demonstrate that the resulting $η$-like state remains robust over broad variations of chemical potential, hopping parameters, and Fermi-surface topology. To detect this hidden staggered order, we propose a phase-sensitive Josephson measurement with a uniform superconductor, where destructive interference suppresses single-Cooper-pair tunneling while preserving two-Cooper-pair processes. This constitutes a charge-$4e$-like Josephson response despite a bulk condensate composed of charge-$2e$ Cooper pairs, providing a direct phase-sensitive signature of the otherwise elusive $η$-like condensate in V$_2$Se$_2$O-family altermagnets.

items.title: Asymmetric multiscalar fixed points from equiangular tight frames
items.summary: In their work on multiscalar RG flows, Rychkov and Stergiou posed the question of whether there exist real fixed points of the one-loop renormalization group for scalar field theories in $d=4-ε$ which respect no extra symmetry beyond the universal $\mathbb{Z}_2$ field inversion. In this note, we report on a construction of a large number of such fixed points in the theory of $22001$ scalar fields, thus resolving the question. The construction uses the geometry of an equiangular tight frame in order to reduce the (up to two-loop) fixed point equation to a two-dimensional space of couplings without assuming any extra symmetry. The main technical hurdle is then to establish the existence of such a frame whose corresponding lines preserve no symmetry. This can be achieved using the Steiner frame construction of Fickus, Mixon, and Tremain.

items.title: Fully Gapped Superconductivity in the Nonsymmorphic Centrosymmetric Superconductor In2Bi
items.summary: The nature of superconductivity in nonsymmorphic In2Bi remains an open question, with ongoing debate over whether it exhibits conventional (BCS-like) or unconventional superconductivity. Here we report the physical characteristics and superconducting properties of polycrystalline In2Bi. Measurements of electrical resistivity, magnetization, penetration depth, and specific heat demonstrate the superconducting transition temperature about 6 K, with a sharp transition in resistivity (Delta_Tc = 0.1 K) and RRR = 57.32, reflecting the high quality of the sample. The upper critical field Hc2(0) obtained from resistivity and magnetization measurements are in good agreement with each other and are smaller than the Pauli limit, suggesting orbital limited mechanism. The coherence length = 35.43 nm, penetration depth = 101.9 nm and electron-phonon coupling constant = 1.05 suggest strongly coupled type-II superconductivity. For T<Tc, Delta_lambda(T) is best described by an s-wave BCS model and does not have any power law dependency with T, which is expected for a nodeless superconducting order parameter. The superfluid density reveals a fully gapped superconductivity with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.02. In the superconducting state, the electronic specific heat is best described by an s-wave BCS model with a gap of 2Delta_0/kBTc = 4.05. All these results from the present study indicate that In2Bi is a typical type-II,BCS-like, strongly coupled, and fully gapped superconductor in the dirty limit.

items.title: Quantum Well Resonant Tunneling Diode Probe of Correlated States in Twisted Bilayer MoS$_2$
items.summary: Moiré superlattices formed in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a versatile platform for exploring emergent quantum phases arising from strong electronic correlations. In this work, we develop a new experimental platform, the quantum well resonant tunneling diode (QWRTD), to probe the electronic landscape of $\approx 56.1^\circ$ twisted bilayer MoS$_2$ (tMoS$_2$). By measuring the differential conductance ($dI/dV_{\text{Probe}}$) as a function of filling factor $ν$ and displacement field $D$, we observe a robust integer insulating feature at $ν= 1$ that persists across the measured displacement field range. Furthermore, we identify a displacement-field-induced fractional insulating feature near $ν= 3/4$ for $D < -75$~mV/nm. Its temperature dependence is consistent with a generalized Wigner crystal interpretation, although the microscopic order remains to be established. These features are also observed in another device with a similar twist angle ($\approx 56.4^\circ$). Our results provide evidence of correlated states in near-AB-stacked tMoS$_2$ and establish QWRTD as a tool for investigating strong correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

items.title: From Surface Reactions to Inhibitor Coverage: A Machine-Learning-Assisted Computational Study of Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition
items.summary: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) enables selective material growth for the fabrication of nanoscale semiconductor devices. Predicting inhibitor coverage is essential for understanding and optimizing surface blocking in AS-ALD. Here, we present a computational workflow combining a pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and apply it to inhibitor adsorption and precursor blocking on amorphous SiO2. Realistic surface models reveal substantial site-dependent variations in reaction energies and activation barriers, with silanol groups serving as the primary adsorption sites for aminosilane and related inhibitors and metal precursors. Coverage simulations show that inhibitors producing identical adsorbed fragments can yield different coverages because the intact molecules impose distinct steric constraints, leading to different accessible site densities and blocking capabilities. Beyond coverage, we highlight the importance of the reactivity of adsorbed inhibitor fragments toward precursors in determining inhibitor stability and blocking performance. Together, these findings demonstrate the need to consider both steric effects and chemical reactivity on realistic amorphous surfaces. Our calculations connect local reaction chemistry with inhibitor coverage and provide a computational basis for understanding inhibition mechanisms and selecting suitable inhibitor-precursor combinations for AS-ALD.

items.title: Predictive Renormalization-Group Theory of Universality Classes in Nonlinear Systems
items.summary: Universal scaling behavior appears across a wide range of nonlinear systems despite substantial differences in their governing equations and physical mechanisms. We develop a renormalization-group (RG) framework that identifies two complementary RG mechanisms underlying such universality. First, scale invariance generates RG fixed points corresponding to asymptotic self-similar solutions. Second, repeated RG transformations eliminate non-scale-invariant irrelevant structures, causing broad classes of equations to flow toward the same fixed points and thereby form universality classes. The framework applies to finite-time singularities, long-time intermediate asymptotics, stochastic Edwards--Wilkinson growth, nonlinear diffusion, density-dependent biological diffusion, and fluid-interface dynamics. In each case, it reproduces known scaling behavior and identifies the associated universality class through explicit irrelevance criteria. A central feature of the framework is its predictive character. Once a scale-invariant fixed point is identified, the theory predicts entire families of nonlinear equations sharing the same asymptotic self-similar solution. While the diffusion class is partially supported by existing mathematically rigorous results, most universality classes identified here have not previously been established and therefore constitute testable predictions. These results provide a unified RG perspective on universality in nonlinear systems and show that universality emerges from the same fundamental RG principles that underlie critical phenomena.

items.title: Adaptive Crack-Tip Localization of Phase-Field Fracture Computations
items.summary: Phase-field models of fracture provide a unified framework for simulating crack nucleation and propagation, but their computational cost remains high because the governing equilibrium and phase-field equations are typically iteratively solved over the entire domain at every staggered iteration. We present an extension of the recently developed adaptive mesh refinement and coarsening framework that localizes not only spatial resolution but also repeated solution effort to a small active patch around the crack tip for linear elastic brittle materials. The inactive exterior is eliminated through a Schur complement and condensed onto the patch interface, and its factorization is reused as long as the patch remains fixed. The phase field is frozen in the exterior, introducing only a small approximation in the crack wake. The method is implemented in FEniCSx and evaluated for quasi-static crack propagation, dynamic crack branching, three-dimensional mixed-mode crack growth, and coalescence of multiple cracks in a unit cell. Across these problems, the condensed formulation reproduces the reference solutions with differences in global quantities below 0.5%, while substantially reducing the number of active degrees of freedom. In the quasi-static surfing problem, wall time speedups increase from 6.9 to 22.8 as the domain size is doubled, demonstrating increasing computational advantage for large-scale phase-field fracture simulations.

items.title: Landau theory and exchange instabilities in Mn$_5$Si$_3$: A case against strain-induced altermagnetism
items.summary: Thin-film Mn$_5$Si$_3$ is a prominent altermagnetic candidate owing to its metallicity, demonstrated anisotropic anomalous transport, and proposed $d$-wave exchange splitting that could enable spin-polarized transport. Its postulated altermagnetic structure has zero propagation vector, unlike the bulk collinear antiferromagnetic AFM2 phase, which orders at the $M$ star. We analyze both phases using Landau theory, first-principles paramagnetic-instability calculations, and Monte Carlo simulations. AFM2 appears in Landau theory as a symmetry-protected inversion-even, permutation-odd mode at a single arm of the $M$ star. At $Γ$, the same intracell pattern belongs to the collinear sector of an $E_{2g}$ order parameter; both phases require higher-order terms for their selection. Disordered-local-moment calculations identify the leading exchange instability at $M$, and the resulting classical Heisenberg model orders at the bulk experimental temperature scale into the orthogonal $3M$ phase favored by single-site entropy. Magnetostructural coupling to $E_{2g}$ deformations favors single-$M$ AFM2 ordering. The estimated homogeneous-strain contribution to the relevant quartic coefficient is about a quarter of the competing entropic term near the bulk transition, while internal $E_{2g}$ relaxations are expected to provide additional stabilization. The $Γ$-point $E_{2g}$ mode, whose Landau theory contains the altermagnetic sector, is substantially weaker and further suppressed by epitaxial strain comparable to that reported for Mn$_5$Si$_3$/Si(111) films exhibiting anomalous transport. The same strain reduces the leading magnetic exchange scale. These results explain the bulk $M$-point instability but strongly disfavor relocating the propagation vector from $M$ to $Γ$ in a moderately strained bulklike Mn$_5$Si$_3$ film, leaving the identity of the Hall-active phase unresolved.

items.title: Chirality-resolved imaging of spin waves with a quantum spin
items.summary: Spin waves carry their propagation direction in the handedness of their circularly polarized stray field, a property inaccessible to scalar magnetometers. In the Damon-Eshbach surface wave of an in-plane magnetized film, the dipolar field above the film rotates with a handedness fixed by the direction of travel. The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre in diamond is an intrinsic polarization analyser: a right-handed field about the NV axis drives one spin transition, and a left-handed field drives the other, in both the ground and the excited state. Here, we exploit the two excited-state transitions, which lie inside the spin-wave band of yttrium iron garnet (YIG), as a pair of chirality channels and image Damon-Eshbach waves in both directions. Because reflection from an etched boundary reverses the handedness, the incident and reflected waves appear as two lines in one spectrum and are imaged separately. In the ground state, the same rule applies, and the selected field drives Rabi oscillations, a route to chirality-selective control of the NV spin by magnons. Reading the two channels gives the direction of a spin wave at one point, without a phase reference. This advances chirality-resolved quantum sensing and provides insight into chiral spin-wave dynamics.

items.title: Pressure-Dependent hcp-to-fcc Phase Transition Path Derived from Exact Lattice Summations over Inverse Power Law Potentials
items.summary: We investigate the phase transition between hexagonal close-packed (hcp) and face-centered cubic (fcc) structures along the Burgers-Bain transformation path at pressures up to several hundred gigapascals. We consider a hierarchy of interatomic potentials, from $(n,m)$-Lennard-Jones potentials to extended Lennard-Jones two-body interactions in terms of inverse-power expansions and the Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body term, alongside density functional theory (DFT) calculations for solid argon. For inverse-power potentials, free energies are evaluated through exact lattice sums and efficient integral representations based on generalizations of the Epstein zeta function to anisotropic interaction kernels, followed by lattice-parameter optimization. This methodology enables an accurate determination of the pressure-dependent Burgers-Bain minimum-energy path and the associated activation barrier for the phase transition. The transformation exhibits pronounced symmetry breaking connecting the Burgers and Bain paths, a feature confirmed by DFT calculations. At high pressure, the hcp-to-fcc activation barrier increases approximately linearly with pressure, owing to the dominant pressure-volume contribution. Including entropy and anharmonic effects yields excellent agreement with experimental temperature-dependent volumes up to the melting point. DFT results also highlight the increasing importance of many-body interactions under compression. Whereas two-body potentials predict that the path passes through the body-centered cubic (bcc) structure only at very high pressures, DFT generally predicts a pathway that bypasses bcc. The Axilrod-Teller-Muto term slightly reduces this discrepancy. Furthermore, DFT performs better at high pressures, where dispersion forces become less important.

items.title: Interplay between high-entropy effects and the superionic transition in fluorite oxides: A liquid-like perspective
items.summary: Minor actinide (MA)-bearing mixed oxide (MOX), a prominent high-entropy ceramic (HEC), is a promising candidate for advanced fast reactor fuels. Using a hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics (MC/MD) approach, we reveal that Np and Am segregation establishes a distinct short-range order (SRO) that induces severe lattice distortion. We uncover a competitive mechanism between localized high-entropy blocking effects and collective superionic dynamics, where the anionic kinetic and structural evolution within the 2000-2800 K range is partitioned and governed by the Tammann crossover temperature and superionic transition temperature. In the low-temperature regime, severe lattice distortions induced by the SRO structures create localized electrostatic and strain-coupled potential wells, which spatially confine the O-ions and lead to their sluggish diffusion. The system exhibits increased dynamical heterogeneity as thermal activation alleviates these structural constraints. Crucially, these localized traps spontaneously transform into a highly interconnected, string-like polyhedral topological network. Driven by the maximization of configurational entropy, this structural change creates low-viscosity transport pathways that trigger confinement-enhanced diffusion. Consequently, a dramatic kinetic inversion occurs, where the O-ion mobility of SRO model surpasses that of random solid solution (RSS) model via an entropy-driven compensation mechanism. Finally, through Gibbs free energy minimization and defect analysis, structural and thermodynamic origins of the superionic transition in HEC are elucidated. This study unveils how local chemical ordering regulates ion transport under extreme conditions, providing theoretical support for the design of high-performance nuclear fuels with both superior radiation tolerance and optimized mass transfer capabilities.

items.title: Coexistence of Griffiths phase and superparamagnetic-like behavior in La-doped antiferromagnetic CaMnO3
authors: N. N. S. V. Rama Raju
items.summary: The coexistence of a Griffiths phase and superparamagnetic-like short range interaction in a single-phase homogeneous manganite is of particular interest because it reveals multiple levels of magnetic clustering generated by disorder and competing exchange interactions. In bulk $\mathrm{La}_{0.19}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.81}\mathrm{MnO}_{3}$, this unusual magnetic state develops in the antiferromagnetic regime, where A-site disorder strongly modifies the local magnetic landscape. Rietveld analysis confirms a single-phase orthorhombic structure, while magnetic measurements establish a Griffiths phase below $T_{\mathrm{G}} = 280\text{ K}$ through the deviation from Curie-Weiss behavior. Superparamagnetic-like behavior persisting from 280 to 370 K further indicates that isolated magnetic clusters remain stable well into the nominally paramagnetic region. The presence of both phenomena highlights the crucial role of disorder-induced exchange randomness in stabilizing complex magnetic states in correlated perovskite oxides.

items.title: ZStar: A unified toolkit for polarization, Born effective charges, dielectric and piezoelectric responses, and infrared and Raman spectra
items.summary: Born effective charge (BEC) tensors link atomic displacements to polarization, thereby connecting lattice vibrations with dielectric response and infrared activity. We present ZStar, an open-source Python toolkit that automates calculations of polarization, BEC, phonons, static and frequency-dependent dielectric response, and infrared and Raman spectra. ZStar supports bulk crystals, two-dimensional materials, one-dimensional structures, and molecules through an integrated workflow for input preparation, execution, and response analysis. Berry-phase polarization and real-space dipoles describe responses along periodic and open directions, respectively. Its unified, symmetry-adapted finite-displacement framework jointly determines BEC and zone-center force constants from the same calculations, improving computational efficiency while preserving numerical accuracy. Strain-response calculations further provide proper piezoelectric coefficients and their internal-relaxation contributions for bulk crystals. In the ABACUS+PYATB route, electronic Hamiltonian data are reused to obtain Raman response without additional self-consistent calculations. Native response implementations from VASP and CP2K are also integrated. Matched infrared/Raman benchmarks against the implemented separate workflows achieve speedups of up to 8.4. An accompanying agent skill provides an agent-friendly interface for workflow integration. ZStar therefore offers an efficient and automated route for exploring polarization, BEC, dielectric and piezoelectric responses, and vibrational spectra across different material dimensionalities.

items.title: Non-Monotonic Exciton Transport Efficiency in Multi-layer Ring-shaped Quantum Networks inspired by Photosystem I
items.summary: Photosystem I (PSI) is one of the most efficient natural photosynthetic complexes and serves as a structural prototype for understanding excitation energy transfer (EET) and designing artificial light-harvesting systems. Here, we construct a multilayer elliptical-conical quantum network inspired by PSI to investigate how antenna architecture affects EET. Excitation dynamics are simulated using the quantum jump approach combined with coherent modified Redfield theory (QJA-CMRT). The transfer efficiency exhibits a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence on pigment density, reaching a maximum of 0.86 at x=6 in the five-layer network. The optimal configuration contains 91 pigments, close to the number of core antenna pigments in natural PSI. Our combined density-of-states and kinetic analyses reveal that this nonmonotonic dependence originates from a trade-off: at low pigment densities, enhanced band overlap promotes energy transfer, whereas at high densities, excessive exciton delocalization compromises funnel directionality and reduces efficiency; the optimal configuration is consequently achieved at x=6. These findings provide insights into PSI antenna organization and offer guidelines for designing efficient artificial light-harvesting systems.

items.title: Representation-Aware Transport-Information Measure for Non-inclusive Discrete Supports
items.summary: Information-theoretic measures for comparing probability distributions are widely used across physics and other fields. When two discrete distributions have non-inclusive supports, however, the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence is in general not directly applicable, and various alternative divergences and distances have been introduced. These measures compare the resulting distributions themselves, but do not generally retain information about the representation transformations by which the discrete distributions are generated from underlying continuous ones. Here we introduce a representation-aware transport-information measure for discrete distributions with non-inclusive supports, formulated based on the standard KL divergence. We consider two continuous reference distributions, each transformed into a discrete representation through its own discretization scheme. Rather than comparing only the resulting discrete distributions or their continuous references, we additionally retain local information associated with the representation-change schemes. The resulting measure can therefore distinguish discrete representations that may have identical discrete probability landscapes but originate from different continuous references or discretization schemes. The construction is based on the transport-information cost of continuous-to-discrete representation in the framework of unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN). UCN provides a non-arbitrary correspondence between the transport cost of discretization as an extrinsic geometric operation and the information-theoretic indistinguishability of nearby continuous distributions, thereby allowing a discrete representation to be associated with a local family of underlying continuous distributions on the statistical manifold.

items.title: Tersoff-NN: Hybrid Machine-Learned Bond-Order Extension of the Tersoff Potential
items.summary: Accurate, robust, and efficient interatomic potentials are highly desirable for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Although machine-learning interatomic potentials can reproduce first-principles potential-energy surfaces with high accuracy, they typically incur higher computational costs than conventional empirical potentials and may be less reliable outside their training domains. We developed Tersoff-NN, a hybrid machine-learning potential for Si, which retains the analytical radial interactions and cutoff structure of the Tersoff potential while representing its environment-dependent bond-order factor using compact neural networks (NNs). Benchmarks for 32,768-atom systems show that Tersoff-NN is 4-12 times faster than the Behler-Parrinello-type NN potentials tested in this study. Tersoff-NN improves the short-range structure of liquid Si relative to the conventional Tersoff potential, closely reproduces the ab initio radial and angular distributions, and reproduces the equilibrium structure of diamond Si and qualitative energetic trends among several crystalline phases. Furthermore, melt-quench simulations reveal a disordered solid with predominantly four-coordinated, tetrahedral-like local environments. Additionally, characteristic reconstruction motifs are retained on Si surfaces despite their exclusion from the training dataset. A direct comparison with an alternative atom-centered bond-order NN highlights the critical role of physical constraints in ensuring dynamic stability. Despite exhibiting comparable validation errors, the selected triplet-based architecture remains stable, while an alternative model exhibits unphysical bond-order growth and atomic collapse. These results confirm that learning only the bond-order term improves the description of diverse Si environments while retaining substantial computational efficiency and enhancing dynamical stability.

items.title: Angular compliance, not amplitude, governs the dielectric response of BaTiO3
items.summary: Soft-mode theory specifies a frequency, not what a local polar unit does. What real-space motion underlies the dielectric response of BaTiO3 therefore remains unclear. Using electric-field-induced molecular dynamics with a machine-learning force field, we show that the permittivity tracks the field-induced angular redistribution of local Ti-O off-centering, not its magnitude. Temperature and biaxial strain modify the local structure through different microscopic routes, yet both dielectric responses collapse onto a common relation with the same orientational descriptor, providing a real-space counterpart to soft-mode behavior.

items.title: Direct Observation of Nanoscale Polarization Switching in HZO Ferroelectrics Using STEM-EBIC
items.summary: We report the experimental observation of discrete ferroelectric switching down to 0.475 nm x 0.475 nm in HfO2-based ferroelectrics using correlated STEM electron beam induced current (EBIC) imaging and nanoscale voltage pulsing. These high-resolution measurements reveal single-domain switching events characterized by abrupt, bi-state transitions with no intermediate polarization states. By mapping polarization-voltage behavior and switching kinetics across thousands of domains, we extract spatially resolved switching thresholds (Emin), switching speeds (tsw), and remanent polarization (2Pr), uncovering robust scaling trends. Larger domains exhibit nearly twice the polarization and faster switching despite higher Emin, while smaller domains switch more slowly at the same field. Sub-domain imaging enables quantification of variation scaling: polarization variation increases linearly logarithmically with area, with inter-domain variation dominating intra-domain variation. Importantly, we show that multi-bit operation arises from the statistical distribution of domain-level switching, rather than partial polarization, enabling distinct and reliable states in devices as small as 0.01 um2. These findings provide a foundational experimental framework for designing scalable, multi-bit ferroelectric memory based on grain- and domain-level heterogeneity.

items.title: Programming the Nonlinear Optics of a Nanoporous Photonic Metamaterial by Confined Crystallization
items.summary: A membrane traversed by a dense array of nanochannels acts as a photonic metamaterial: with channels far smaller than the wavelength of light, the optical response is set by the architecture rather than by the constituent materials. Here each nanochannel is turned into a nonlinear optical meta-atom by filling anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) with benzil (BZL), a noncentrosymmetric molecular crystal, and the crystallization pathway programs their orientation. In free-standing membranes every channel solidifies independently, the orientations remain uncorrelated, and the effective second-harmonic generation (SHG) response is nearly polarization isotropic; its magnitude follows a core - shell model in which an optically inactive interfacial layer of 2.6 nm reduces the active volume of each meta-atom, reproducing on bare alumina the value previously found on alkyl-grafted silica and indicating a host-insensitive limit. Seeding crystallization from a bulk benzil layer instead aligns the meta-atoms over submillimeter domains and produces a macroscopically anisotropic effective susceptibility. Channel diameters from 32 to 270 nm span the transition out of the subwavelength regime, and the anomalous directional SHG emission reported here is confined to the metamaterial limit. Confined crystallization thus offers a route to nonlinear optical metamaterials whose effective susceptibility tensor is written during processing.

items.title: Generalized length-gauge time-dependent Liouville equation
items.summary: The length-gauge (LG) time-dependent Liouville equation is a major workhorse to simulate ultrafast dynamics. The equation features the commutator between the density operator $\hatρ$ and the position operator ${\bf r}$, $\langle n{\bf k}|[{\bf r},\hatρ]|m{\bf k}'\rangle$, where $|n{\bf k}\rangle$ and $|m{\bf k}'\rangle$ are Bloch states for bands $n$ and $m$ at crystal momenta ${\bf k}$ and ${\bf k}'$, respectively. This commutator has two irreconcilable versions: Kohn and Luttinger (Phys. Rev. ${\bf 108}$, 590 (1954)) have two partial derivatives with respect to ${\bf k}$ and ${\bf k}'$, but Aversa and Sipe (AS) (Phys. Rev. B ${\bf 52}$, 14636 (1995)) have one partial derivative and one Dirac delta. For several decades, this outstanding discrepancy has received little attention. Here, we show that the generalized LG time-dependent Liouville equation has two partial derivatives, but no Dirac delta. Physically, the ${\bf k}$-off-diagonal matrix elements of the position operator provide a channel by which the electric field generates ${\bf k}$-off-diagonal matrix elements for $\hatρ$ in LG. The discrepancy emerges when the position matrix is assumed to be diagonal in ${\bf k}$. Consequently the AS' equation is a limiting case of our generalized Liouville equation, where the relative momentum ${\bf Q}$ between two states is ignored. Our numerical test reveals that the ${\bf k}$-diagonal formalism yields qualitatively different results and underestimates both energy absorption and polarization by a factor of 7. Our study establishes a general formalism for the length-gauge time-dependent Liouville equation and opens the door for future research on the ultrafast time scale, while prior results based on the ${\bf k}$-diagonal only equation may need to be revisited.

items.title: Metastable polar order and phase competition in Carpy-Galy LaTaO4
items.summary: Carpy-Galy LaTaO$_4$ undergoes a structural sequence linking the antipolar monoclinic $P2_1/c$ ground state and the polar orthorhombic $Cmc2_1$ phase through an incommensurately modulated regime. First-principles calculations identify a metastable polar monoclinic $P2_1$ phase as a commensurate intermediate in the phase-transition landscape. As a common subgroup of $P2_1/c$ and $Cmc2_1$, $P2_1$ provides a symmetry-connected route between the established polymorphs. Mode-resolved energy surfaces for these symmetry-breaking pathways show that coupling between the respective primary order parameters and an isosymmetric relaxation stabilizes the $P2_1$ minimum along both pathways. Consequently, the $P2_1/c\rightarrow P2_1$ transformation has a finite energy barrier, while a restricted soft-mode model retains competing $P2_1$ and $Cmc2_1$ basins over an illustrative range of harmonic stiffness. Lattice-metric and neutron-diffraction comparisons indicate a shared displacement character between the calculated commensurate state and the experimental IC-o modulation, supporting the use of $P2_1$ as a commensurate structural reference for IC-o. Finally, composition-dependent energetics suggest chemical routes for tuning polar-antipolar competition.

items.title: Basin-volume distributions in monodisperse particle packings -- the soul of memory
items.summary: Mechanically stable packings of $N$ particles in $d$ dimensions lie at the minima of an $Nd$-dimensional potential energy landscape. Starting from random initial particle positions, the system can relax using gradient-based optimization until it arrives at one of the equilibrium states; all initial conditions that end at the same minimum belong to the same catchment basin. We measure the distribution of the catchment basin volumes for indistinguishable monodisperse soft spheres in both $d=2$ and $d=3$. Ordering the basins at each system size, $N$, according to their volume, $P_N(n)$, from the largest at $n=1$ to smaller at larger $n$, we find a very wide distribution of volumes which is similar in both dimensions: $P_N(n) \approx A_Nn^{-α}$ with $α\approx 1$ which, in our most favorable cases, extends over $7$ decades. We explore aspects of the connectivity of the basins, show that their structure is highly contorted, and demonstrate how these results may be used to understand the imprinting of memories in cyclic strain studies of solids.

items.title: High mobility narrowband-emissive organic semiconductors
items.summary: This work proposes a synergistic control strategy of molecular packing and transition dipole moment orientation for achieving high mobility narrowband-emissive organic semiconductors.

items.title: Iron electronic delocalization enables catalytic selective trisilyla-tion: beyond steric hindrance
items.summary: Abstract The efficient synthesis of sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes, particularly the synthetically valuable 1,1,2-trisilylalkenes, remains a longstanding challenge due to significant steric hindrance encountered during the bond formation. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed trisilylation of ynamides that leverages iron electronic delocalization to modulate the character of double bonds toward that of single bonds, effectively mitigating steric constraints during the reaction. This strategy enables a regioselective and controllable synthesis of 1,1,2-trisilylated alkenes, trans -1,2-disilylated alkenes, and monosilylated alkynes under mild conditions with high efficiency. Notably, the method allows for late-stage functionalization of biologically relevant molecules, offering a valuable platform for the structural diversification of alkynes. In addition, the resulting multisilylated intermediates undergo diverse downstream transformations, granting access to a broad array of otherwise elusive tetrasubstituted silylalkenes. Experimental and computational studies reveal that monosilylalkynes serve as key intermediates, with β -N elimination, double migratory insertion, and reductive elimination steps likely involved in the catalytic cycle. This work provides fundamental insights into the construction of sterically hindered chemical bonds via base metal catalysis and underscores the potential of iron to unlock unconventional reactivity through electronic delocalization effects.

items.title: Amplitude mode in Eliashberg superconductors
items.summary: In the BCS theory of superconductivity the amplitude (Higgs) mode is degenerate with the pair-breaking threshold: its frequency coincides with $2Δ$, so it is an edge singularity rather than a true collective mode. This is why after a sudden weak perturbation at $t=0$ its oscillations decay algebraically as $1/\sqrt{t}$. We show that the retardation effects due to the phonon dynamics in the strong-coupling theory lift this degeneracy. The Higgs mode detaches from the pair-breaking edge $2Δ_g$, set by the spectral gap, and becomes a sharp subgap excitation. We determine its frequency from the longitudinal pair susceptibility evaluated directly on the real frequency axis, using the Eilenberger equations for Migdal--Eliashberg theory with the Einstein phonon spectrum. The response of the mass renormalization supplies at least two fifths of the displacement, and possibly all of it: with it switched off, the binding falls below the resolution of the calculation. Its consequences, however, are significant because a percent-level shift transfers about a quarter of the spectral weight of the amplitude channel out of the two-quasiparticle continuum into a discrete energy level. What experiment sees is therefore not the displacement itself but its consequence: amplitude oscillations that persist instead of decaying as $1/\sqrt{t}$.

items.title: Time-dependent integrable quantum field theories with dynamical boundaries
items.summary: We present a general method to construct and solve time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories on finite intervals from autonomous scattering and reflection data. Spatial homogeneity forces the spectral labels of right- and left-moving particles to be affine with a common slope, so bulk and boundary couplings sample one spectral trajectory. A complete round trip shifts the spectral labels and gives boundary quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equations. The Yang--Baxter and reflection equations provide local consistency, while boundary-qKZ flatness provides global consistency. We reconstruct the local Hamiltonian by Cayley inversion of the bulk and boundary matching matrices. We apply the construction to rational $SU(N)$ scattering with fundamental boundary impurities and to an $O(3)$ model with a spin-$\tfrac12$ impurity. For the $SU(2)$ impurity, we construct explicit boundary-qKZ solutions as lattice sums of off-shell boundary Bethe vectors and recover the static open-chain Bethe equations when the drive rate vanishes

items.title: Emergent Discrimination and Polarization in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: We study theoretically how discrimination and polarization can emerge in a population of learning agents. Each agent uses an adaptive linear decision layer to map a language-model embedding of an issue to a binary opinion and maintains an evolving estimate of how much it trusts every other agent. Through pairwise interactions, agents update both their decision weights and trust estimates using an online Bayesian rule derived from teacher-student learning over a noisy channel. In-context-learning experiments with large language models qualitatively reproduce the predicted opinion and trust updates. We then assign each agent one of two arbitrary group labels, A or B, and model group bias by allowing a fraction $f_b$ of agents to shift its perceived agreement with each message by a strength $b$, a bias steering prejudice, depending on whether the sender and receiver share a label. We use order parameters from statistical mechanics to connect these local dynamics to collective states and transitions. Starting from uniformly random initial conditions, simulations reveal a rich phase diagram in the $(b,f_b)$ plane, comprising four collective states: spin-glass frustrated out-group favoritism, nondiscriminatory polarization, discrimination with opinion alignment, and discrimination without opinion alignment. Which state emerges depends on both the strength and prevalence of the bias. These results show how simple local learning dynamics can generate qualitatively distinct forms of polarization and discrimination, underscoring the need for population-level safety analysis of multi-agent systems. They also suggest measurable order parameters for characterizing analogous collective states in human societies.

items.title: Chirality-induced spin selectivity as a nonequilibrium effect: a unified test of competing mechanisms
items.summary: For two decades, the origin of Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS), the spin polarization of electrons by nonmagnetic chiral systems without magnetic fields, has remained unsettled. Here, we establish a single exact rule defining the fundamental conditions for the effect: in nonmagnetic, time-reversal-invariant conductors, all measurable CISS signals are time-reversal odd and vanish near equilibrium, proving that structural chirality alone is insufficient. By evaluating leading theoretical mechanisms across four levels of nonequilibrium transport, from coherent classical driving to fully non-Markovian quantum baths, we verify this selection rule to machine precision. We show that coherent chiral vibrations generate substantial collinear polarization (up to 10 percent across 0.5-6 THz) that reverses with handedness, whereas incoherent vibrations yield under 1 percent, and non-Markovian bath memory further suppresses the signal. The chiral geometry first makes the electronic motion chiral by accumulating orbital angular momentum; spin-orbit coupling (SOC) then converts that into spin. CISS therefore acts as both a spin polarizer and a spin filter, the latter an order of magnitude weaker. The polarization grows with molecular length and then saturates, matching trends reported for DNA and peptides. Reversing the drive converts decaying spin into a handedness-locked charge-current pulse (inverse-CISS). We find that once the system is driven, the polarization magnitude scales with an effective spin-orbit coupling: making heavy atoms and curved light-atom backbones indistinguishable at equivalent effective SOC. This enables us to chart how geometry, driving field, and length separate those routes.

items.title: Photon-stimulated decay of $χ$-matched ancillas causes unheralded bit flips in bosonic codes
items.summary: Bosonic codes often read out their syndrome with a transmon ancilla whose computational levels $g$ and $f$ have equal parity and matched dispersive shifts: a decay $f\to e$ is then heralded and leaves the code intact, while the direct $f\to g$ is forbidden by parity. We show that the photons of the code open this decay at first order in the ancilla's decay rate. Dressing by the code mode lets the charge noise that limits the ancilla's $T_1$ drive a photon-stimulated Raman decay $|f,n\rangle\to|g,n+1\rangle$, at $(n+1)(χ_{ge}/2g_{01})^2$ times the $f\to e$ rate for a smooth noise spectrum. When the matching is set by the detuning, the decay costs $\approxΓ_{fe}/α$ per gate and photon, whatever the coupling strength; a deliberate mismatch or matching by a drive lowers this cost, and a qubit ancilla has no such channel. The opened decay is unheralded and flips a cat with probability $\approx 1/2$; being first order, it overtakes the second-order double decay $f\to e\to g$ as the ancilla improves. In a microscopic model of the Ocelot repetition cat code, it makes the bit-flip floor of the gates grow linearly with the cat size, by a factor 1.2-1.7 from four to ten photons, which would limit the noise bias to $\sim 10^3$. The published gate data end at four photons and do not yet test this growth.

items.title: On a relationship between grain boundary free energy, grain boundary segregation, and grain boundary diffusion
items.summary: We present a detailed analysis of the universal relationship between grain boundary (GB) free energy and GB self-diffusion coefficient derived by Borisov et al. (1964). This relationship was expressed by a simple equation that was used in many publications to predict GB energies on the basis of experimental diffusion data. Meanwhile, the physical assumptions and approximations underlying the Borisov model are poorly understood. As a result, the Borisov equation was often used outside its intended limits.
